General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: A decades-old mystery about light could hold the key to faster internet

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Light can carry vast amounts of information, but developing faster and more efficient optical communication systems requires precise control over how it travels.
  • Recent findings suggest that A research team led by KAIST has uncovered detailed information about how light moves through BTO and how much of it the material absorbs.
  • According to recent reports, KAIST (President Choongsik Bae) announced the results on November 8.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Light can carry vast amounts of information, but developing faster and more efficient optical communication systems requires precise control over how it travels. Scientists have now made an important advance in understanding barium titanate (BTO), a promising material that could help improve the performance of future devices that transmit information using light.

Recent findings suggest that A research team led by KAIST has uncovered detailed information about how light moves through BTO and how much of it the material absorbs. These properties have been difficult to measure accurately for decades because of the crystal's complicated internal structure. The newly introduced findings provide engineers with a more reliable foundation for designing optical devices that minimize signal loss and support faster data transmission.

According to recent reports, KAIST (President Choongsik Bae) announced the results on November 8. The research was led by Professor Min Seok Jang of KAIST's School of Electrical Engineering, working with Professor Harry A. Atwater's group at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), the Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS), and U.S.-based J.A. Woollam Co. Together, the researchers examined how BTO interacts with light across wavelengths extending from the ultraviolet to the far-infrared.

Why Barium Titanate Could Transform Optical Communications.

Sources indicate that one of BTO's most valuable characteristics is its ability to change how it affects light when electricity is applied. This behavior, called the Pockels effect, gives the material a strong electro-optic response and makes it especially attractive for optical modulators. These components convert electrical information into signals carried by light, making them important building blocks for advanced communication systems.

In a recent development, however, producing reliable devices requires a detailed understanding of two fundamental optical properties. The refractive index describes how light travels through a material, while the extinction coefficient indicates how strongly the material absorbs it. Engineers need both measurements to predict how light will behave inside a waveguide, a structure designed to direct light along a specific path, and how much of the optical signal may be lost.

According to recent reports, getting consistent measurements from BTO has been surprisingly challenging. The material can contain multiple microscopic regions, called domains, in which the crystal structure points in different directions. Because these regions interact with light differently, measurements of an entire sample can combine several distinct responses. This has contributed to widely conflicting reports of BTO's optical properties over many decades.

Solving a Decades-Old Mystery About Light.

To overcome this problem, the researchers used a sophisticated measurement method known as Mueller matrix spectroscopic ellipsometry. The technique examines how the polarization of light changes when light reflects from or passes through a material, allowing scientists to investigate its optical behavior in detail.

It has been revealed that rather than relying on crystals containing a complicated mixture of differently oriented regions, the team studied two types of single-crystal samples with relatively consistent domain orientations. This approach helped minimize overlapping optical responses and allowed the researchers to identify the material's underlying properties more accurately.

It has been revealed that their measurements spanned wavelengths from 190 nanometers (nm) to 40 micrometers (μm), covering an exceptionally broad range of light from ultraviolet to far-infrared. Since a material's optical behavior changes with wavelength, the scientists divided the spectrum into three regions and applied a different analytical approach to each. This revealed how BTO's refractive index and light absorption depend on both wavelength and crystal orientation.

Industry observers note that the researchers also investigated a particularly important range in which BTO allows nearly all incoming light to pass through. By combining ellipsometry with separate measurements of light transmission, they detected extremely low absorption, determining extinction coefficients of approximately 10-5 in the 2-10 μm wavelength range. These precise values will help engineers estimate how much light is lost as it travels through or remains confined within optical components.

According to recent reports, in another advance, the team developed a way to predict the combined optical behavior of crystals containing multiple domains. Their method uses the orientations of those domains and the proportion of the crystal occupied by each to calculate the material's overall response to light.

Opening the Door to Faster Data Transmission and Quantum Technology.

The results could make the development of future optical devices more predictable and efficient. With accurate information about BTO's behavior, engineers can model how light will travel through components of different shapes and dimensions before manufacturing them. They can also better estimate absorption losses, potentially reducing the need for repeated prototypes, costly redesigns, and extensive testing.

According to recent reports, the potential benefits extend beyond conventional optical communications. BTO could also play an important role in devices that produce light at different wavelengths, as well as photonic circuits that use light to process quantum information. Such technologies depend on controlling light with exceptional precision.

"This study reveals the optical response of barium titanate, which had long remained unclear, and provides a reliable reference for how the material interacts with light," said Professor Min Seok Jang.

Jang also emphasized that the findings could contribute to optical communication devices capable of transmitting data faster while reducing light loss. The improved understanding of BTO may also support the development of quantum photonic technologies, where precise manipulation of light is essential.

The study was published online on October 20, 2026, in ACS Photonics. Jiwon Kang, a Ph.D. candidate in KAIST's School of Electrical Engineering, and Dr. Nina Hong of J.A. Woollam Co. served as co-first authors. Professors Min Seok Jang of KAIST and Harry A. Atwater of Caltech were the corresponding authors.

According to recent reports, funding was provided through the Culture, Sports and Tourism R&D Program administered by the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA), with support from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism; the Basic Science Research Program administered by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF), with support from the Ministry of Education; the Ministry of Science and ICT; and the U.S. Air Force Office of Scientific Research (AFOSR).

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.
  • There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

In a recent development, ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

According to recent reports, at the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Recent findings suggest that swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the newly introduced regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

It has been revealed that the aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing fresh free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

Industry observers note that while you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free revision, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech organization and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.

The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Company’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly swiftly.

As it right now stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.".

The concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre firm who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

Tech Report: For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (851 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, how often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout.
  • The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues.
  • It has been revealed that depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, how often you exercise may matter more for your mental health than how hard you push yourself during a workout. A large study of Norwegian college students found that those who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety one year later. The findings suggest that maintaining a consistent exercise routine could be particularly crucial for supporting mental well-being.

The research, published in the open access journal PLOS One, was conducted by Michael Grasdalsmoen of Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and his colleagues. Their results point to the potential benefits of exercising regularly rather than focusing primarily on longer or more demanding workouts.

Why Exercise Habits Matter for Mental Health.

It has been revealed that depression, anxiety, and other common mental health conditions are among the leading causes of disability in young adults worldwide. The college years can be an especially challenging period as students adjust to upcoming academic, social, and personal responsibilities. Identifying everyday behaviors that may help protect mental health is therefore an crucial research priority.

Sources indicate that although previous research has linked regular physical activity to better psychological well-being, many young adults remain physically inactive. Scientists have also had relatively limited evidence about how exercise habits relate to the development of mental health conditions over time, particularly when those conditions are evaluated using standardized diagnostic tools.

To investigate this relationship, Grasdalsmoen and his team followed 10,460 full-time students enrolled in higher education in Norway. Participants ranged in age from 18 to 35.

Recent findings suggest that at the beginning of the study, students completed questionnaires describing their exercise habits, including how frequently they worked out, how strenuous their activities were, how long they exercised, and how many total hours they were active each week. One year later, they completed a self-administered diagnostic assessment designed to identify common mental health disorders.

Exercise Frequency May Matter More Than Intensity.

The researchers found that students who reported lower levels of physical activity were more likely to meet diagnostic criteria for anxiety or depression one year later. However, not every aspect of exercise showed the same relationship with mental health.

In a recent development, exercise frequency emerged as a particularly consistent factor. How often students exercised was more reliably associated with their later mental health than the intensity of their workouts or the amount of time they spent exercising.

According to recent reports, the researchers also identified differences between men and women. Among women, lower exercise intensity was associated with a greater likelihood of anxiety and depression. Among men, spending fewer total hours exercising each week showed a stronger association with these conditions.

Overall, the likelihood of common mental health disorders decreased as weekly exercise increased, with this pattern continuing up to approximately 10 hours of physical activity per week.

The results also support the World Health Organization's recommendation that adults complete at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each week.

Regular Exercise Could Help Support Student Mental Health.

Industry observers note that taken together, the findings suggest that exercising consistently may be especially valuable for reducing the likelihood of anxiety and depression among college students. Rather than concentrating exclusively on workout intensity or duration, maintaining a regular routine could be an important part of supporting mental health.

However, the researchers emphasize that their observational study cannot establish a direct cause-and-effect relationship. Although students who exercised more regularly tended to have better mental health outcomes, the results do not prove that exercise itself prevented depression or anxiety.

Even with this limitation, promoting accessible opportunities for physical activity could be a useful part of broader efforts to improve student well-being. Such efforts may be especially relevant for students who are beginning to experience mental health difficulties or symptoms that have not yet reached the threshold for a clinical diagnosis.

Sources indicate that the authors add: "Our findings show that students who engage in regular physical exercise are at lower risk of developing common mental disorders over time. These findings highlight the importance of making physical activity an accessible and natural part of student life.".

"Mental health among students is a growing public health concern. Our findings suggest that supporting students to be physically active may contribute to better mental health and should be recognized as an vital part of a healthy learning environment.".

According to recent reports, funding: The SHoT study was financially supported by the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research (2017) and the Norwegian Ministry of Health and Care Services (2016). Neither funding organization participated in designing the research, collecting or analyzing data, deciding whether to publish the findings, or preparing the manuscript.

7 Unique JRPG Mechanics We Want in Modern Releases

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1219 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that JRPGs are evolving in a fairly consistent way.
  • Today, I want to explore some JRPG mechanics I would love to see in modern releases.
  • When I first played Vagrant Story, I barely knew what I was doing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that JRPGs are evolving in a fairly consistent way. While modern titles keep several staples of the genre, such as a fixed story, a focus on character development, innovation in the battle system, and some wacky progression systems, sometimes it feels like they leave behind certain mechanics that could be put to great use today. Many JRPGs of yesteryear featured unique mechanics that were either never re-explored, or, if they were, remained confined to indie games and flew under the radar of many players.

Today, I want to explore some JRPG mechanics I would love to see in modern releases. Most are battle-related, though a few, if properly implemented, could expand exploration and even improve how the game's systems interact. That is not to say they have never appeared in other games throughout the years, but I would love to see them become much more mainstream.

When I first played Vagrant Story, I barely knew what I was doing. When chaining attacks, you can aim at enemies' limbs, yet all I ever did was try to go straight for the head or body to defeat the foe as fast as possible. How naive I was, because against bosses, that mindless strategy never paid off, especially if I was not wielding an appropriate weapon.

This mechanic of targeting different body parts has popped up in other JRPGs, though usually you can only hit distinct areas when an enemy is preparing a specific attack. I would love to see a JRPG reuse this mechanic exhaustively, letting players willingly target different enemy limbs and trigger distinct tactical outcomes.

According to recent reports, one of Star Ocean's greatest strengths is its Item Creation system. To me, gaining levels wasn't about learning latest combat skills, but it was all about earning points to invest in Customization and unlock new crafting potential, whether forging an endgame weapon at the start of the game or diving into other side activities. Still, the most entertaining feature, even at the cost of my relationship with my party members, was Pickpocketing.

In a recent development, leveling up your Pickpocketing skill lets you steal from every NPC in town and score the wildest variety of items. The sheer thrill of not knowing what you would get, whether a simple consumable or an insanely overpowered piece of gear, was endlessly fun and had me making the rounds through town as if I were living inside GTA. As mentioned, doing so affects how your party members perceive the protagonist, so if you are aiming for a specific ending, watch out for the consequences of your actions.

According to recent reports, this entry is less about battle mechanics and more about dungeon delving. As much as I love modern JRPGs, especially for their evolution in combat gameplay, narrative, and character development, I feel some are still a bit lacking in the level design department. Too many dungeons are simply streamlined corridors, featuring an occasional puzzle that solves itself before you even begin thinking through the solution.

According to recent reports, plenty of classic JRPGs boasted incredible level design, but if I had to highlight just one, it would be Wild Arms. This series blended the interactive tools of action-adventure games and let the scope of exploration expand incrementally. Moreover, acquiring new tools encouraged backtracking and re-exploring older dungeons, much like a Metroidvania, to hunt down hidden treasures.

I never had much contact with Sega consoles growing up, which led me to neglect their JRPG catalog for quite a while. I played Phantasy Star IV fairly recently, and during my playthrough, a friend told me to set up Macros using specific skills while emphasizing that the execution order mattered. So I complied, and when I stepped into battle, oh boy, what a beautiful surprise.

Industry observers note that for those who don't know, depending on the sequence in which you cast spells and skills, they fuse together to unleash an entirely new combo attack. It is a deeply entertaining combo system that later surfaced in future JRPGs like Breath of Fire IV. It feels distinct from two characters simply chaining standard turns together, because there is a real sense of mystique in discovering the combinations, and I will confess that without a GameFAQs guide, I never would have figured them all out. Still, it is pretty amazing and elevated turn-based combat to new heights.

According to recent reports, staying on the topic of skill combos, Chrono Trigger pulled off something similar yet distinctly its own. If two or three party members mastered specific techniques and had their ATB gauges filled simultaneously, they could execute a Double or Triple Tech, each carrying a unique effect. The very first time I discovered this, as I imagine most players did, was with Crono and Lucca's Fire Whirl. A whole upcoming world of tactical possibilities opened up in that exact moment.

Sources indicate that chrono Trigger pushed the concept even further, and just when I expected the game to stick to Double Techs, the JRPG introduced Triple Techs. I don't know about you, but I built my entire party around these Techs, and luckily, nearly every character paired well with the rest of the roster. Triple Techs were slightly more restrictive, yet they still allowed for remarkably efficient setups, especially when hunting for Techs capable of healing the entire party at once.

Industry observers note that breath of Fire is my favorite JRPG series, and within it, Breath of Fire III stands as my absolute favorite entry. Whenever people ask me why, a massive part of my reasoning rests on its Gene splicing system, a feature Breath of Fire IV dropped for reasons I still don't understand, which was a real shame. I loved transforming into dozens of distinct dragons, even if Ryu and Fou-Lu's half-dragon forms looked awesome in their own right.

Industry observers note that essentially, you discovered Dragon Genes scattered across the world and could combine up to three at once to transform Ryu into wildly different dragon forms, each boasting unique strengths and abilities. The thing is, I don't necessarily need the exact Gene system back, but I would love a transformation-focused JRPG where characters can shift forms mid-battle and completely alter the flow of combat. Even better if those transformations feature distinct variations that actively reward exploration.

I know there are many, many caveats surrounding the progression mechanics of Final Fantasy VIII, though I feel the bulk of player complaints stems from the Draw system rather than the Junction system itself. There is a historical reason behind that, as Hiroyuki Ito, creator of both the ATB and Junction systems, left the Final Fantasy VIII team before finalizing the battle mechanics to direct Final Fantasy IX, leaving his original vision somewhat incomplete.

Sources indicate that just imagine what it could have been if fully realized. The Junction system is remarkably dynamic. Beyond simply slotting spells to boost each character's raw stats, you could attach status ailments to basic physical attacks, build elemental resistances, tailor one character toward magic and agility while turning another into a pure strength powerhouse, and so on. Pair that flexibility with specialized commands learned through Guardian Forces, and what appears on the surface to be standard turn-based combat suddenly gains deep strategic layers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their aims for the shooter making some big promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.

Top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. It's a roguelite mode, one that's playable in co-op, though a lack of details at this current time doesn't make it clear as to whether you can run it solo or not. The season's trailer, which you can have a gander at below, gives off the impression that you'll have to complete particular tasks before exfiltrating like you normally do. I'm sure we'll learn more in time.

The previously promised social space will be coming with this enhancement too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the latest runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

What will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few upcoming weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, big ole alien enemies to take on.

You've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is at the moment slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).

Sentinels have signed Briton Georgio 'keiko' Sanassy from NRG as the final starter in their 2027 VCT Americas lineup. The move pairs him again with former NRG teammate brawk as Sentinels try to return to international events after missing them all in 2026.

The Sentinels lineup for 2027 now reads johnqt, brawk, OXY, canezerra and keiko. Zellsis rounds out the group as sixth man. He came back to the organisation on 7 November in that role and as a content creator. Contract lengths were not disclosed.

Industry observers note that sentinels called keiko ‘bloody brilliant’ in its announcement. Riot’s VALORANT Esports account then shared the news and described him as ‘the finishing touch’ on the lineup.

Sheep Esports first reported the move on 8 November, citing sources, and noted keiko was expected to play controller. The same report had brawk on initiator and johnqt on sentinel.

Industry observers note that the signing ends a rapid rebuild. OXY arrived on 2 November and brawk a day later. canezerra followed on 6 November. Four days after that, cortezia and Reduxx were released.

Only a few hours before joining Sentinels, brawk had ruled out staying at NRG.

keiko’s NRG spell ran from 12 November 2025 to 21 October 2026. He finished third at Masters Santiago 2026. He also placed third in both VCT Americas Stage 1 and Stage 2. At Champions 2026 he finished joint fifth to sixth.

That spell ended once Champions was over. NRG told him he would not be kept for the following year, keiko said on X on 21 October. He was then free to look for a latest team as a restricted free agent.

Sentinels reached no international event in 2026. The team went out of that year’s Kickoff in the bottom four. It then missed the playoffs in both Stage 1 and Stage 2. Adding a player with that run of results is consistent with a side trying to close the gap promptly.

In a recent development, keiko was born on 12 September 2003. He grew up in and around London. He played competitive Fortnite before switching to VALORANT. His VALORANT career began at UK sides WYLDE, from May to August 2022, and BONK, from October to December 2022. He then joined Apeks from January to November 2023. That year he won the Challengers Rising Stars award. Team Liquid followed, from November 2023 to November 2025. His move to Sentinels places a British player at the centre of a rebuilt Americas contender.

The newly introduced lineup’s next test is the Americas Kickoff. Partner teams are guaranteed a place only at Kickoff. The Americas has eight partner teams, and all of them receive direct invitations to its event. Four further places go to non-partner teams.

It has been revealed that the 2027 Kickoff events will be played in person in each international region. One of the non-partner places in the Americas will be decided by a Last Chance Qualifier in São Paulo on 17–18 December.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The results were especially striking for people with prediabetes.
  • "We know weight loss can improve metabolic health in people who are obese," notes Samuel Klein, the study's corresponding author at Washington University School of Medicine in St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A ketogenic diet may offer significant health benefits beyond weight loss, according to a new clinical trial that compared three popular approaches to eating. Researchers found that people following a very low-carbohydrate, high-fat diet experienced substantially greater reductions in liver fat than those eating Mediterranean or low-fat diets, even though all three groups lost similar amounts of weight.

The results were especially striking for people with prediabetes. After just four to five months on a ketogenic (or "Keto") diet, approximately half of the participants no longer met the diagnostic criteria for the condition. The findings, published in the journal Cell Metabolism, suggest that the types of foods people eat can influence metabolic health in ways that extend beyond the number of pounds they lose.

"We know weight loss can improve metabolic health in people who are obese," notes Samuel Klein, the study's corresponding author at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, Missouri. "Our data suggest that if you have high liver fat content and prediabetes, reducing carbohydrate intake can have crucial therapeutic effects on metabolism beyond just weight loss alone.".

Comparing Keto, Mediterranean, and Low-Fat Diets.

Sources indicate that an estimated 40% of American adults have obesity, a condition associated with increased risks of type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, and other health problems. Doctors frequently recommend dietary changes to help patients lose weight and improve their metabolic health, which refers to how effectively the body manages energy, blood sugar, and fats.

It has been revealed that three commonly recommended approaches are low-carbohydrate diets, low-fat diets, and Mediterranean diets. Although each can support weight loss, researchers have been uncertain whether one offers additional metabolic advantages when the amount of weight lost is roughly the same.

According to recent reports, these eating patterns differ substantially in their nutritional makeup. Low-carbohydrate approaches, including Atkins and ketogenic diets, restrict carbohydrate consumption, while low-fat diets may obtain as much as 70% of their calories from carbohydrates. The Mediterranean diet emphasizes plant foods such as vegetables, nuts, and olive oil, along with moderate amounts of fish and dairy. Ketogenic diets, meanwhile, can include considerable amounts of fat from animal products, including saturated fat.

According to recent reports, to compare their effects, Klein and his colleagues recruited 42 adults with obesity, prediabetes, and fatty liver disease. Prediabetes occurs when blood sugar levels rise above the normal range but have not yet reached the threshold for type 2 diabetes. Fatty liver disease involves excess fat accumulating inside liver cells, which can interfere with the body's ability to regulate metabolism.

A Controlled Clinical Trial With Similar Weight Loss.

In a recent development, participants were randomly assigned to follow one of three diets: ketogenic, Mediterranean, or a low-fat diet emphasizing plant-based foods. To ensure that participants followed their assigned eating looks, the research team supplied all their meals and arranged weekly consultations with a dietitian.

The diets had sharply different proportions of carbohydrates and fat. In the ketogenic group, carbohydrates accounted for just 4% of daily calories, while fat supplied 73%. The Mediterranean group received 50% of its calories from carbohydrates and 35% from fat. The plant-forward group consumed 70% of its calories from carbohydrates and 15% from fat.

According to recent reports, researchers adjusted calorie intake individually so that participants across all three groups lost approximately 10% of their starting body weight. Reaching this target took about four to five months.

Recent findings suggest that by the end of the intervention, every group had experienced meaningful reductions in body fat and improvements in insulin sensitivity. Insulin is the hormone that helps move sugar from the bloodstream into cells, where it can be used for energy. Greater insulin sensitivity makes it easier for the body to maintain healthy blood sugar levels.

However, the similarities between the groups largely ended there.

Keto Diet Reduces Liver Fat by 67%.

The ketogenic diet produced the largest improvements in several important indicators of liver function and metabolic health.

Participants following keto experienced an average 67% reduction in liver fat, compared with a 45% reduction in both the Mediterranean and low-fat groups. Because the groups lost comparable amounts of weight, the difference suggests that carbohydrate restriction may influence liver fat through mechanisms beyond weight loss alone.

To investigate these effects, the researchers collected blood samples repeatedly over a 24-hour period, allowing them to observe changes in hormones involved in energy metabolism.

The ketogenic group demonstrated the greatest increase in glucagon, a hormone that helps regulate the body's energy supply and promotes the reduction of fat stored in the liver. Participants on keto also experienced the largest decrease in insulin levels, another change that can help reduce liver fat accumulation.

One result was particularly unexpected. Despite getting nearly three-quarters of their calories from fat, the keto participants did not show an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels during the study.

"The most surprising finding was that participants in the ketogenic diet group didn't experience an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels despite consuming the most fat," indicates Max Petersen, the study's first author at Washington University School of Medicine.

Half of Keto Participants No Longer Had Prediabetes.

Recent findings suggest that the benefits extended beyond liver fat. After the weight-loss intervention, approximately 50% of participants assigned to the ketogenic diet no longer met the criteria for prediabetes. By comparison, that milestone was reached by 29% of those on the Mediterranean diet and just 7% of those following the low-fat, plant-forward diet.

These differences are notable because prediabetes signals an elevated risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Bringing blood sugar levels below the prediabetes threshold is an notable improvement, although it does not necessarily mean the condition has been permanently reversed.

Sources indicate that the findings also highlight a potentially vital distinction in weight management: losing weight and improving metabolic health are closely connected, but they are not necessarily the same thing. The composition of a diet may affect how the body handles blood sugar, stores fat, and responds to hormones, even when weight loss is similar.

According to recent reports, researchers emphasize the growing importance of understanding these effects as powerful upcoming obesity treatments become more widely available. GLP-1 medications, which act on hormone pathways involved in appetite and blood sugar regulation, have transformed the treatment of obesity by helping many patients achieve substantial weight loss.

"GLP-1-based medications have revolutionized the therapy of obesity. We now have a very effective pharmacotherapy for achieving significant weight loss," Petersen states. "But in addition, our study indicates that the specific composition of the diet can give you added benefits.".

In a recent development, although the trial was relatively small and lasted only four to five months, its carefully controlled design offers evidence that dietary composition can play an important role in metabolic health. Longer studies involving more participants will be needed to determine whether the benefits persist and how different diets compare over time.

The research was supported by the National Institutes of Health and the Foundation for Barnes-Jewish Hospital.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain company finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are currently technically and legally preparing themselves.

Recent findings suggest that IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business complications they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's vital to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.".

Zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he noted.

It was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.".

In a recent development, essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

10 Most Unhinged NPC Interactions in GTA 6

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1497 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Grand Theft Auto series is known for its absurdity, and it gave us some many memorable moments throughout its run.
  • Leonida is no stranger to the strange and weird, and since the first trailer for GTA 6, you could tell that it would be a place that is off the wall.
  • If you are planning on taking a trip across Leonida, whether it is by fan boat or sports car, get ready to see some strange happenings all across the state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Grand Theft Auto series is known for its absurdity, and it gave us some many memorable moments throughout its run. However, Grand Theft Auto 6 is taking the absurdity to a latest level, with NPCs that are far more over-the-top than ever before.

Leonida is no stranger to the strange and weird, and since the first trailer for GTA 6, you could tell that it would be a place that is off the wall. There are old people running away from the cops on mobility scooters, people you can spot in… unfortunate positions, and even some strange moments that catch you completely off guard.

If you are planning on taking a trip across Leonida, whether it is by fan boat or sports car, get ready to see some strange happenings all across the state.

Shortly after you start up GTA 6, Brian will ask you to stop by a girl named Mandy’s house to collect the rent. This sounds like a fairly simple job, and there shouldn’t be anything that you have to worry about with it.

Of course, nothing is ever simple in GTA, and you have to put up with a girl who desperately needs a tall glass of Jason. She is perhaps the thirstiest character I have ever seen, and she consistently tries to lure Jason into a compromising position.

She goes so far as to catch Jason off guard by wearing next to nothing while he tries to fix her sink. Plus, you find out she clogged the sink herself to get Jason to come over. She has issues.

One of the many side characters in GTA 6 is Cal. He is Jason’s friend, and he is also one of the most absurd characters you will run into throughout the game. He constantly has something to say, and it is often hilarious.

It has been revealed that during one of the nights early on in the game, Cal comes over and installs a JoyStation for Jason. The two of them rearrange the house, and then they have a few drinks while they chat through the night.

Sources indicate that it ends with things getting a bit wild and the pair end up spooning in the bedroom. You awaken to a strange sight, and it fits Cal’s character perfectly.

Industry observers note that it is normal for NPCs to get angry at you while you are driving in a Grand Theft Auto game. After all, you probably don’t drive very well and have little regard for the rules of the road. Well, the NPCs in GTA 6 take things to a upcoming level.

Sources indicate that sometimes, when you bump into a vehicle while driving around Leonida, the NPC will get so angry that they chase you down. This can go on for a while, and the result is often the NPC plowing into your vehicle to stop you.

According to recent reports, after this, they get out and assault you for hitting their car. It is a much bigger reaction than NPCs had in GTA 5 and it is something that fits in the land of Leonida.

In a recent development, bert is a strange character who is obviously meant to signify the less reasonable members of the right-wing political ideology. He appears next to Mandy’s house with his pants down, flashing his genitalia to Mandy’s neighbors while screaming at them.

It is a strange sight to behold, but what is even more strange is that the landlord demonstrates up to fight Bert. The man gets out of his truck, starts yelling at Bert, and tells him to get off his property.

Sources indicate that however, things take a turn when they realize that they see eye-to-eye, with both of them wearing shirts of a similar fashion. Bert then gets offered a job while his family jewels are blowing in the wind.

There are plenty of random events that can happen in GTA 6, especially when you are exploring Vice City. Some of the NPCs around here get a little bit crazy. One such way is through their driving.

Sources indicate that one of the game’s random events involves a car that comes careening down the highway only to take a sharp turn, flip, and get destroyed. It is a wild turn of events that you can get involved in.

If you stop to see if everyone is okay, the NPCs involved will freak out about the crash and high tail it out of there before the cops come. This leaves you with a bag of drugs that you can take to a stash house. Pretty convenient.

According to recent reports, during one of the main story missions, Jason and Lucia have a night on the town, which leads them to a fun time in Vice City with Mattia. The night culminates in a massive party in a hotel room. During this party, however, Lucia gets separated from Jason.

While separated from Jason, you get to wander into various hotel rooms, and some of them are not for the faint of heart. For instance, one room has you walking in on a man dressed head to toe in leather, with a woman who is …inserting something into his body that is usually exit only.

It is a very unexpected scene that will catch you entirely off guard, and it is also one of the most unhinged things I have seen in a game between two consenting NPCs.

There are some NPCs who are into doing some wild stuff in Leonida, and I am not just talking about wild in the bedroom like the NPC from earlier. Instead, I am talking about some extreme stunts. This one might also count as an easter egg, but it is an interesting interaction.

Industry observers note that at the top of a radio tower, which just so happens to be one of the tallest spots in the game, you can find an influencer who is climbing the tower. She can be found hanging off of it, and if you interact with her, you will question why she is doing it.

Recent findings suggest that she will respond by telling you that she climbed the tower because another influencer named Kelly Explores did it. Either way, it is weird and makes the list.

Industry observers note that there are some pretty desperate NPCs in Grand Theft Auto 6. Some of them are willing to go to great lengths to make some money and get ahead in life. One guy in particular is willing to risk it all by robbing a store, but his weapon of choice isn’t a pistol, shotgun, or assault rifle.

Instead, it is a banana. That’s right, a banana. You can happen to walk into a store and see a man threatening the clerk, but while the store clerk can’t see the man’s weapon, you can clearly see that he is holding a banana behind his back.

It has been revealed that you can put a stop to the man by threatening him, or you can watch the scene play out. Either way, it is pretty hilarious and pretty unhinged of him to attempt a robbery with produce as a weapon.

Sources indicate that it is hilarious the type of people who think they can get away with something in GTA 6. For instance, there are some elderly folks who think that they can just rob people on a mobility scooter.

Industry observers note that there are a few outcomes that this can have, but it all starts with a woman with a mullet driving around on a mobility scooter. She will pull a gun on someone, who will end up giving her their money.

According to recent reports, she will then pull a gun on you, and you can choose to give her the money, wait for the cops to arrive, and see her get arrested, or you can decline. If you decline, she will curse at you and drive away. Better yet, you can just push her over and take her money.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a chance that you will run into some NPCs in the Grassrivers who got their van stuck in the mud. This kind of thing happens to everyone, and so you may be inclined to help them out. After all, they will actually ask for your assistance.

Recent findings suggest that if you help them out, they will reward you with some drugs and be on their way. Nothing too special, unless you end up looking in the back of the van, in which case, things get wild.

If you walk up to the back of the van, one of the men will tell you to stop, but it is too late. Inside, is a tiger, and opening the doors will cause it to jump out and pounce on one of the NPCs, taking his face clean off.

#75233. Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1305 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1305 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Plastic is used in everything from food packaging and water bottles to children's toys, largely because it is considered chemically stable and unlikely to react with its surroundings.
  • As larger plastic objects fragment into microplastics and even smaller nanoplastics, the amount of exposed surface area increases dramatically.
  • Researchers at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley identified the chemical processes behind this phenomenon in a fresh study published in Nature.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Plastic is used in everything from food packaging and water bottles to children's toys, largely because it is considered chemically stable and unlikely to react with its surroundings. However, new research suggests that this assumption may not hold when plastic breaks down into extremely small particles.

As larger plastic objects fragment into microplastics and even smaller nanoplastics, the amount of exposed surface area increases dramatically. Scientists have now discovered that these newly exposed surfaces can interact with water in unexpected ways, producing reactive molecules that may harm living cells.

Researchers at Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley identified the chemical processes behind this phenomenon in a fresh study published in Nature. Their findings challenge the longstanding idea that microplastics are simply passive fragments of material.

"As plastic fragments into smaller and smaller particles, its surface area increases enormously. Then microplastics change the water that surrounds them, generating high-energy, reactive radicals (reactive oxygen species, ROS) that very likely contribute to biological damage that we see in animals and potentially in humans as a result of microplastic exposure," remarked Wei Min, a Columbia professor of Chemistry and Biomedical Engineering.

Why Microplastics Could Be Dangerous Inside the Human Body.

The discovery raises crucial questions about what happens when microplastics enter the human body. Blood and cells contain large amounts of water, creating conditions in which these tiny particles could continue participating in chemical reactions.

Rather than remaining inactive after exposure, microplastics may generate reactive oxygen species, often called ROS. These highly reactive molecules can damage biological structures, including components of cells and tissues. The findings offer a possible explanation for some of the harmful effects associated with microplastic exposure, although they do not establish that this process causes specific diseases in humans.

The research builds on earlier work by Min's laboratory that helped reveal just how widespread microscopic plastic contamination has become.

In a widely reported 2024 study, the Columbia researchers developed a laser-based microscopy technique capable of detecting extremely small plastic particles. Using this technology, they found an average of approximately 240,000 detectable plastic fragments in a single liter of bottled water (mostly nanometer-sized plastic, nanoplastics). That was 10 to 100 times more particles than previous estimates had suggested.

The discovery helped draw greater attention to the presence of microplastics and nanoplastics throughout the food system.

Growing Concerns About Microplastics and Human Health.

Since that earlier research attracted widespread attention, the potential health consequences of microplastic exposure have become an increasingly crucial public health issue.

In 2026, the federal government rolled out a $144 million initiative focused on addressing toxic microplastics in the human body. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency also added microplastics to a federal list of contaminants that may be of concern in drinking water, marking their first appearance on the list.

Meanwhile, studies published in major scientific journals, including the New England Journal of Medicine, Nature Medicine, and Nature Health, have reported associations between exposure to microplastics and nanoplastics and serious conditions such as heart attacks, strokes, dementia, and brain tumors.

Industry observers note that however, an important question has remained unanswered. If plastic is generally considered chemically inert, how might these microscopic fragments contribute to biological damage?

The newly introduced findings identify a previously overlooked chemical pathway that could help researchers understand these potential health risks.

Industry observers note that "Our research found that when microplastics interact with water, as they do when they're in bottled water, or when they're absorbed into our bloodstream, they spontaneously generate what we call reactive oxygen species (ROS)," said Naixin Qian, a postdoctoral researcher in Wei Min's lab who helped lead the research. "ROS are textbook examples of the kinds of molecules that can damage animal and human tissue.".

How Water Triggers Harmful Chemical Reactions.

One of the most surprising aspects of the discovery is that water plays an active role in the reaction.

Many plastics are hydrophobic, meaning their surfaces repel water. When water encounters these surfaces, the molecules and electrically charged particles near the boundary can behave differently than they do in ordinary water.

The researchers found that these interactions can encourage electrons to move between chemical species, allowing highly reactive radicals to form. As plastic fragments become smaller, their greater surface area provides more locations where these reactions can occur.

"Water is a key active player here, rather than just a spectator. It's integral to making these microplastics reactive. Water molecules become chemically active when they come into contact with plastic, which is hydrophobic. Contact between the water and plastic creates an environment that facilitates electron transfer, and the formation of reactive radicals. When plastics fragment into smaller particles, their increasing surface-to-volume ratio creates more of these chemically active areas," Min stated.

To investigate the process, the Columbia researchers performed chemical and biological experiments. Their collaborators in Professor Teresa Head-Gordon's laboratory at UC Berkeley used theoretical calculations and computer simulations to examine the interactions between plastic surfaces and water at the molecular level.

Recent findings suggest that the Berkeley team developed a theoretical explanation showing how hydroxide ions, which are negatively charged particles, can become concentrated in the layers of water immediately surrounding a water-repelling plastic surface. In this environment, the ions can more readily lose electrons and form hydroxyl radicals.

According to recent reports, hydroxyl radicals are particularly reactive chemical species capable of damaging biological molecules. Their formation provides a possible link between the physical breakdown of plastics and the biological effects researchers have observed.

Could the Discovery Lead to Safer Plastics?

Understanding the chemistry involved could eventually help scientists develop plastics that are less likely to generate harmful reactive molecules when exposed to water.

"Our fundamental work that the most hydrophobic microplastics interacting with water can drive chemical reactivity could ultimately lead to upcoming engineering solutions by redesigning the chemistry of these commodity plastics to reduce the toxic outcomes on health and the environment," said Head-Gordon.

Industry observers note that the implications also extend beyond human health. Microplastics can enter rivers, lakes, and other waterways through industrial waste, wastewater, and everyday activities. The newly identified chemical reactions could influence aquatic organisms and ecosystems exposed to these particles.

According to recent reports, co-author Beizhan Yan of Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory emphasized that microplastics can originate from numerous sources, including plastic manufacturing facilities and laundromats. Everyday processes, such as heating materials in a microwave or leaving bottled water exposed to sunlight during storage, can also contribute to the formation of tiny plastic particles.

It has been revealed that "This work has significant implications for environmental and human health," said co-author Beizhan Yan of Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory. "In certain environments, such as discharges from plastic manufacturers and laundromats, microplastics can form and enter aquatic environments. This work also indicates that radicals can form on hydrophobic plastic surfaces in water, which could affect ecosystems and human health following exposure. In addition, various uses and processes in our daily lives can generate microplastics, including microwave heating, sunlight exposure of bottled water during storage. This foundational work provides a potential pathway for understanding their health impacts.".

Recent findings suggest that by revealing that microplastics can actively alter the chemistry of surrounding water, the research adds a new dimension to concerns about plastic pollution. It also establishes a potential mechanism for investigating how these widespread particles interact with living systems, while opening the door to strategies for reducing their environmental and health risks.

#75232. Even our bunch of diehard PC gamers aren't that bothered by 30 fps in GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1893 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pcgamer ↗ Open Full Page

Even our bunch of diehard PC gamers aren't that bothered by 30 fps in GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer.
  • It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.
  • Industry observers note that GTA 6 certainly does that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for a bunch of performance snobs, we are a surprisingly forgiving bunch at PC Gamer. Yes, if you try to insult XCOM, you're going to get a slap, but we've only just started playing GTA 6 (well, some of us) and we're mostly over the whole 'only runs at 30 fps' thing already.

It turns out, while we're happy to part with our money to buy expensive components to hit higher frame rates (and earn the right to brag about it), we're also just as happy to settle for less when a game does a lot of other things exceptionally well.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 certainly does that. That's the impression I get from most members of the team that have played it so far. Though if Rockstar is listening, when you do get around to our precious PC version, we'd love nothing more than 4K60—maybe more.

Sources indicate that I will no doubt appreciate frames above 100 fps when GTA 6 comes to PC. Heck, I'd even just appreciate going up to 60 fps. But in my handful of hours with the game thus far, I just have simply not been that bothered by it. Be it smart ways of masking low frames, or even just the slower, methodical control approach of the game, I'm less frustrated with my PS5 running the game at around 30 fps than I was recently playing Phantom Blade Zero at well above 40 fps on a handheld PC.

According to recent reports, maybe that's down to the world having a little bit of magic to it, maybe it's the engrossing tone and atmosphere, maybe it's just because it looks so darn pretty. Maybe it's because I haven't got to the game's most hectic moments yet and haven't really needed to hit a headshot with my console unable to keep up with me. I'll tell you how I'm getting on in another fifty hours. Cool, see you in three days, then?

Industry observers note that I was dreading playing GTA 6 on my OG PS5—a dusty ornament that's been chilling out in my living room this last year doing absolutely nothing. I've got a nice gaming PC in my office (RTX 4090, Intel i9 13900K, 32 GB RAM), so it's been a long time since I've had to deal with games dipping below 80 fps. I have been spoiled.

The second I got to control Lucia, my fears seemed justified. Everything just felt sluggish. But that feeling didn't last. I played GTA 6 for around 5 hours last night (I am very tired) and I haven't thought about the frame rate once since that initial section. Whether I'm getting into shootouts with coke smugglers, speeding through the Keys at night, or bouncing around at sea, GTA 6 looks great and feels great.

I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth.

I can still tell this isn't 60 fps, but it is smooth. I'm sure I've encountered drops, but crucially I haven't noticed them. Sure, it's inevitably going to look better and run better on PC, but the lower performance on my PS5 rapidly ceased to be an concern, and I'm not regretting playing it on console.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is the kind of game where an uncapped framerate would be nice, but it doesn't feel essential. Like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it—a game I also played at 30 fps before it launched on PC—its pacing is measured. It feels designed around the limitations of the consoles it's launching on, prioritising detail and depth over twitch-based combat and precise interaction. It's exactly what I'd expect from a modern Rockstar game. Also like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it, I still feel the sense of longing for what this game will look like on PC. Make no mistake: the version at the moment available is a preview for what GTA 6 will be at its best. It's great, but those who can wait will be treated to a superior experience.

It's also possible that the 30 fps cap will feel more restrictive once the online mode arrives—whenever that will be, and in whatever form it takes. It's one thing to handle a lower framerate within Rockstar's meticulously created campaign. It's quite another in a lobby of other players. If GTA 6's multiplayer is even half as chaotic as the current GTA Online, every frame is going to count.

As I was booting up GTA 6, I was expecting to be annoyed by the game's paltry frame rate. And I was—at first. Much like Fraser, during the opening scene with Lucia, I saw my fears come to life on the big screen in front of me. Objects juddering and blurring as I swung my camera around in the cramped cell. Did I just waste £80 on GTA 6 on PS5 when I should've held my nerve for the PC version?

According to recent reports, truth is, the frame rate has had nowhere near as much of a negative impact on my experience while I've been traversing the Floridian wilds as Jason. In part, I think that's because there's a lot more going on, as cars, shops, people, and poultry fly past me as I break most state, federal and ethical laws. That reduces the chance of my eyes fixating on any one object and noticing the adverse effects of the game's lower fps, or the ways Rockstar has gone about covering for it.

Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil.

Low fps is one thing, but motion blur is the devil. That's not just my opinion, that's been scientifically verified (sorta) to be the opinion of PC Gamer readers. Admittedly, some motion blur may be required when the frame rate is this low, so I have played around with a few settings in GTA 6 to find the perfect balance. I'd heard through the grapevine that higher-than-default motion blur (default is 3, goes up to 10) may be preferential to reduce the more obvious juddering that is present at low fps, but whoever says that is no friend of mine. I've landed on setting motion blur to 1 on the standard PS5, as it feels the cleanest overall. I wouldn't blame anyone for turning it off entirely, especially on a more powerful console where the frame rate may not dip as much.

Recent findings suggest that of course, I do agree with the rest of this lot: in an ideal world, playing the PC version, I'd be pushing a much higher frame rate with motion blur banished to the abyss where it belongs, and a full selection of graphics settings to tinker with to my liking. Yet, to my surprise, I'm not as much of a console version curmudgeon as I thought I'd be.

In a recent development, is the low frame rate noticeable? Yep. Would it be better at a higher frame rate? Also yep. Is the low frame rate a detriment to my overall enjoyment of GTA 6? Only a smidge.

Industry observers note that I don't consider myself much of a framerate snob, but I'll admit I was side-eyeing GTA 6's 30fps just a little bit. Well, that was before the game came out. Now that I have my hands on it, with roughly six hours spent lollygagging around Leonida? I'm hardly noticing it, though I'll most definitely be appreciating a smoother experience once the PC version rolls around.

Like Jacob stated, motion blur definitely seems to be masking it somewhat—and I am traditionally a motion blur hater, so it's taken a little getting used to—but I'm genuinely pleasantly surprised at the balance Rockstar has managed to strike between a smooth performance and a dense, rich world.

GTA 6 taught me that I don't much care about frame rates as much as I expected. I got to start playing it a few weeks ago and didn't have anyone to compare notes with, and my first thought was: Huh, they got it to run at 60 fps after all! It all felt very smooth, even when I realized it was 30 fps after all. It was only a bit later I started noticing very occasional drops, like while driving during a gradual lighting chance from day to night.

I think it being consistent is key.

But that's really infrequent. I think it being consistent is key. I'm on a PS5 Slim, by the way, not a Pro. That's not to say I still can't wait to see it at higher frame rates when it finally gets to PC. But 30 fps feels mostly fine for the time being.

It has been revealed that it was actually spending a lot of time playing with handheld gaming PCs and laptops with integrated graphics that reminded me I shouldn't give as much of a shit about frame rate as I do. Largely that obsession is born of having high-end hardware sat in my desktop PC, but when crashing around with a range of handhelds I'm reminded of the old days when 30 fps was a target for PC games, too.

Sources indicate that it's also reminded me that it really depends on the game engine, as well. Not every 30 fps game looks the same as other 30 fps games. And Rockstar has obviously worked incredibly hard to make sure that 30 fps looks as good as it possible can. Otherwise why would that be a solid target for all four of the console platforms it's released on?

For the most part Rockstar has done a great job of keeping things smooth.

I've been playing GTA 6 on the Xbox Series X, which does suffer from the odd dip in frame rate, too—though oddly I've only really noticed it during canned animations the characters do starting certain actions, such as opening the trunk of a car or pulling something out of it. But for the most part Rockstar has done a great job of keeping things smooth. And not just by using motion blur. For the record, I'm running that at 0 and have not looked back.

Recent findings suggest that I'm less happy about the vignetting that I'm getting around the darkened edges of the screen, but I'm playing it blown up on a 4K projector so I've got plenty of screen real estate to enjoy. And I have been, thoroughly enjoying it, I mean. The frame rate, for me, hasn't got in the way once.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

According to recent reports, this comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony stated that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Industry observers note that bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

Sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

Sources indicate that for those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was declared back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a latest name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

Alan gets stronger by eating his own cooking.

According to recent reports, in an RPG, you’d expect to become stronger by hitting things, but in Kemco’s latest, you do it by eating your own cooking (abs are made in the kitchen, as the saying goes). Leingham Tavern Story: Alan and the Time Goddess is out now on the App Store and Google Play. It’s a dungeon crawler and a restaurant sim at the same time, and there’s an orphanage to save on top.

Recent findings suggest that that orphanage is the whole reason you’re doing any of this. It’s about to close down, and Alan and his mates reckon a busy tavern will make enough money to keep it going. Which means heading down into dungeons for ingredients.

Recent findings suggest that you can go back to these every day, picking things up from gathering points and getting into turn-based fights with whatever monsters are lurking about. You’ll want better gear for the fights and you’ll want levels too, but like I mentioned, you get most of those from eating when you’re back.

According to recent reports, back at the tavern, you can buy recipes, and you can also mix ingredients yourself and see what you get. There are more than 800 dishes to find. There’s a field out the back for growing vegetables too, plus a fishing spot for when you fancy a break (apparently you can catch something you weren’t expecting, though I’ve no idea what).

Then there’s running the place, which is what actually keeps the orphanage going. Once a few dishes are on the menu, you open the doors, and from there it’s a case of changing what you cook to suit the season and whatever customers are into at the time, and working out which of your staff should be doing what. Leingham Tavern Story only comes in English and Japanese, and there’s no controller support either.

Leingham Tavern Story: Alan and the Time Goddess is out now on the App Store and Google Play for $9.99.

If you’re after something else to sink a few hours into, check out our list of the top RPGs on Android.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed.
  • Revision 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.
  • Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Revision 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios unveiled it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

Sources indicate that the patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

Sources indicate that the other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.
