Sources indicate that nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

It has been revealed that unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

In a recent development, another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

It has been revealed that this time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since they released The Outer Worlds 2 around this time last year, the world has rather turned upside down for Obsidian. The studio lost a chunk of staff to Microsoft's mass layoffs and have pivoted to making a fresh Fallout game as a smaller group shoved underneath Bethesda in Xbox's corporate structure.

It has been revealed that given all that, The Outer Worlds 2's two-part story expansion is likely arriving in vastly different circumstances than those the studio might've imagined when they began sketching out DLC looks. Part one of the expansion, dubbed Side Effects Guaranteed, is set to release early next month.

According to recent reports, 'Oof, that looks a lot like it's been given what could turn out to be a death spot parked right in the aftermath of GTA 6's initial launch on consoles' is what I thought when I first saw that Side Effects Guaranteed's launch date is December 2nd. That mentioned, Obsidian have also made clear that a second DLC in the two-part narrative expansion to the sci-fi RPG is set to follow in spring 2027. So if this does turn out to be the end of the series, with a third Outer Worlds game currently looking very unlikely following the substantial upheaval I mentioned in the intro, at least it won't risk being totally obscured by a Rockstar crime game-shaped eclipse.

As for what this first dose of extra Outer Worlds 2 has in store for December, Obsidian summed it up as follows:.

Industry observers note that as you pursue the cure and set course for Elysium, an area home to former subjects of base game authoritarian collectivist faction the Protectorate, you'll be faced with the choice of whether to side with Gordon Hazen or Algernon Lankester. Both are agents of black market smuggling organisation Sub Rosa, with one sounding like the goody-two-shoes diplomatic type and the other wanting to "exploit the subjects for his own personal gain". Sounds more Saturday morning cartoon than serious RPG story with serious choices, but that's always tended to be how The Outer Worlds leans.

In a recent development, rounding out the expansion are new enemies, gear, flaws which give your character build a funky twist, and a bumping up of the level cap from from 30 to 36. Fittingly given I'm writing this on Skyrim's 15th birthday, one of the new flaws is named 'Must Have Been the Wind' after the meme of enemies in the likes of Bethesda and Obsidian's games returning to chill mode after being shot in the face with an arrow or facing some other obvious sign they're under attack. To encourage folks to dive back in, The Outer Worlds 2 is getting options to respec your character's skills and edit how many skill points are dished out per level up via an revision alongside Side Effects Guaranteed.

In a recent development, as much as I'm resigned to the series' likely fate as Obsidian return to Fallout and won't pretend The Outer Worlds 2 was great rather than good, I'm still hopeful it can go out with a bang in these two expansions, if indeed this is the studio's last trip to space for the foreseeable future. It's worth noting that if you bought The Outer Worlds 2's premium edition, these expansions are included as part of it and so will come to you at no extra cost.

Nvidia's board of directors has reportedly met to decide whether to remove the company's embattled CEO Jensen Huang, as news of a second extramarital affair has come to light.

Per the Wall Street Journal, the board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang following reports he allegedly participated in another affair with an executive who worked for him.This followed the revelation of his affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which prompted a organization-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation into whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

The board's decision has yet to be made, but there are three expected outcomes. Either Huang stays with the manufacturer and continues as Nvidia leader, despite the controversy or he is replaced as CEO, or he quits. Nvidia's share price dropped following reports of this meeting taking place.

Sources indicate that if Huang is fired - and perhaps even if he isn't - it's likely to severely disrupt Nvidia's operations. Huang co-founded Nvidia and led it to become one of the world's most valuable companies - it interchangeably wears that crown, alternating with Apple. Replacing Huang might change the tech giant's focus.

Recent findings suggest that regardless, Nvidia is under major scrutiny right now because of Huang's actions. There are particular concerns around the company's chips being imported to China despite trade bans. Gamers Nexus produced a documentary on the Nvidia AI GPU Black Market, detailing much of this.

Breaking: Avoiding Steam Machine this Black Friday? Here's what other mini PCs can actually get you for your cash

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1600 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Steam Machine is now "checkout-ready" according to Valve, but with a $1,049 starting price for the 512GB base model (and that $1,349 rate on the 2TB version up for debate in the near-future), there's a problem for those who don't want to break four figures on a fresh system.
  • According to recent reports, that's where the well-established (but recently far more popular) world of mini PCs comes in.
  • These devices have been finding themselves in more homes this year, as increased prices of the best gaming PCs and even cheaper components have pushed both those after a productivity and gaming solution towards more budget-friendly alternatives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Steam Machine is now "checkout-ready" according to Valve, but with a $1,049 starting price for the 512GB base model (and that $1,349 rate on the 2TB version up for debate in the near-future), there's a problem for those who don't want to break four figures on a fresh system.

According to recent reports, that's where the well-established (but recently far more popular) world of mini PCs comes in. Whether you want more options further down the price range or you're after something with more graphical grunt, these compact PCs prove it's not just Valve producing ready-to-go gaming machines that don't take up floor space.

These devices have been finding themselves in more homes this year, as increased prices of the best gaming PCs and even cheaper components have pushed both those after a productivity and gaming solution towards more budget-friendly alternatives.

Sources indicate that I've spent the last few months road-testing mini PCs from Geekom to Asus, spanning the full price range. Right at the bottom, boxes like the $499 Geekom A5 2027 Edition will gear themselves heavily towards indie titles and retro emulation. At the top, you'll find full dedicated GPU options spanning up to the RTX 5070.

It's worth noting that the Windows operating system won't give you that living-room-console ease of the Steam Machine, but instead opens you up to more versatility around launchers and OS compatibility.

Like you, I was curious to see what these tiny little rigs could actually conjure - and you'll find out exactly how each price point fared in my benchmarks just below.

I've spent the last six months running my everyday workflow through mini PCs across a range of brands, testing every compact rig I can get my hands on in whatever games they allow for. Around that, I've also been testing and reviewing gaming laptops on GamesRadar+ for the last six years, using similar components in different configurations every two weeks.

The best deal you'll find on the budget Geekom A5 2027 Edition right now sits with Amazon. A $50 discount on the original $549 takes us to $499 this Black Friday. While prices have been jumping since the start of the year here, that's cheaper than it has been since July. This one's dropped to around $400 earlier in 2026, though.

The Geekom A5 2027 Edition is a productivity machine first and foremost. The AMD Ryzen 7 7730U under the hood is designed to run efficiently, quietly, and with minimal power draw. That means it can hum away in the background without breaking the bank, but it also sweeps away a lot of the power more demanding games require.

I was still curious to see how gaming actually fares at the lower end of the budget. In short, this thing will run your indie Steam library no problem. If you prioritize smaller titles, you'll get on just fine here and likely kick yourself if you opt for anything more expensive. Retro emulation runs nicely as well, if that's your jam.

That's about as far as you'll get, though. Shadow of the Tomb Raider, an older "double-A" release that doesn't tend to make too many gaming laptops sweat, neared smooth framerates only with resolution set to 720p and settings dropped to their lowest. Medium can just about squeak by on a smaller screen at 28fps.

According to recent reports, the same story is true of Cyberpunk 2077, the major guns test. Without frame generation you're looking at 27fps at 720p here, though we do jump up nicely to 45fps with a little extra help.

These more demanding games are playable. They run. You can even get over 30fps if you make larger sacrifices - a perfectly decent position at the budget end of the spectrum. They're just not going to feel nearly as good as they might slightly further up the price scale.

The GMKTec K8 Plus has dropped under $700 in the past, but today's $170 discount is a starting point. I'd keep a close eye on this one as Black Friday progresses, rather than diving in straight away now - this one stands to wriggle under that $700 threshold if we're lucky.

The GMKTec K8 Plus upgrades your processor to the Ryzen 7 8845HS, adds an Oculink connection for future eGPU upgrades, and includes extra support for more monitor displays. That's a set of upgrades that will set you up for more demanding games a lot better than the budget-minded Geekom A5.

According to recent reports, in practice, that means solid 40+fps in Shadow of the Tomb Raider at both medium and high settings in 1080p, with Cyberpunk 2077 managing 41fps in medium as well. You've got a lot more breathing room here, as well as power ceiling that allows for that FHD resolution.

Mid-range "double-As" are more-than possible with a few tweaks, and more demanding titles are within reach here as well.

Ultimately, this is your all-rounder. It's powerful enough to represent solid value for money across chunkier games while still giving you room to grow with that eGPU connection and easily upgradeable innards.

I have one major caveat from my testing, though. You might need to upgrade the Wi-Fi card when you buy it. Internet was incredibly slow for me during testing, far slower than any other device on my network. There's something funky going on behind the scenes here, but customers have reported a fresh card solves the problem.

According to recent reports, the Geekom A9 Max is available with that Ryzen Ai 9 HX470 chipset, 2TB SSD and 32GB RAM for $1,499. Again this one has been cheaper this year so far, so it's worth watching over the next week. Still, it's been locked in at $1600 since August.

Industry observers note that the Geekom A9 Max is a step up in price compared to our more budget-friendly alternatives, and overtakes the 2TB Steam Machine cost. So what's in it for you?

Industry observers note that this is actually a very similar value proposition to the Steam Machine, hitting 30+fps in Cyberpunk 2077 at 1440p Medium settings without any frame generation help. Adding frame-gen into the equation, and it's easy to speed well past that 60fps threshold. It's a step up where more demanding games like CD Projekt Red's open world are concerned, though improvements further down the scale are more measured compared to the GMKTec further up.

Industry observers note that what's going to separate these two rigs, though, is what else you want to do with your PC. The Geekom A9 Max can match the Steam Machine in overall performance, but it also adds a whole workstation into your purchase.

Recent findings suggest that this is where Windows plays its most key card in this trip into mini PC land. While you won't have that console-like operating system, you'll have everything you need for demanding productivity tasks and workflows on top of that gaming performance. It's the better option for those not just buying a gaming device, but rolling their purchase in with their work machine.

We're down to a brand-upcoming record-low price on the RTX 5070 Asus ROG GR70 mini PC this Black Friday, with the $2,599 configuration shedding $300 from the final price. This one's only ever dipped just below $2,500 in previous sales, though it's still one of the most expensive mini PCs on the market.

The largest, and most expensive, mini PC I've had on my test bench so far, the Asus ROG GR70 isn't a budget alternative to the Steam Machine but an additional investment in more demanding PC games. This is a full system, with a dedicated RTX 5070 graphics card humming away inside, and some of AMD's most powerful processors up top as well.

Industry observers note that I tested the AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX3D / RTX 5070 version with a whopping 64GB RAM under the hood. That's a particularly expensive configuration in today's rates, one that comes in at around $2,800.

For that kind of cash, you can easily pick up one of the best gaming laptops or a cheaper full-tower PC - so the ROG GR70 is only for those specifically seeking a miniature form factor.

It has been revealed that how did it go? Unsurprisingly, for a rig often twice the price of the Steam Machine, pretty damn smoothly. Triple-figure frame rates are the norm for most Triple-As in high settings at FHD, while we're still well above 60fps in everything at 1440p as well.

According to recent reports, that's performance that's going to blow the Steam Machine out the water, but it's still tracking behind other RTX 5070 counterparts. The value of this beast compared to an RTX 5070 gaming laptop or desktop PC doesn't quite stack up - you'll need to know you're in it for the miniature footprint for this premium pick to make sense.

We're also rounding up the best gaming handhelds and best gaming tablets for more ways to play this holiday season.

Managing Editor of Hardware at GamesRadar+, I originally landed in hardware at our sister site TechRadar before moving over to GamesRadar. In between, I've written for Tom’s Guide, Wireframe, The Indie Game Website and That Video Game Blog, covering everything from the PS5 launch to the Apple Pencil. Now, i'm focused on Nintendo Switch, gaming laptops (and the keyboards, headsets and mice that come with them), PS5, and trying to find the perfect projector.

Hell Let Loose: Vietnam Reveals the Star of Its Next Patch

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (747 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since its release earlier this year, Hell Let Loose: Vietnam has gotten plenty of praise for capturing the grit and horrors of the jungles of Vietnam.
  • The dev team over at Expression Games has taken that to heart.
  • The next major release for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, upgrade 2.0, is bringing the FN FAL into the fray, specifically in its British version that saw combat in the region.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since its release earlier this year, Hell Let Loose: Vietnam has gotten plenty of praise for capturing the grit and horrors of the jungles of Vietnam. At the same time, the game has also been on the receiving end of criticism for its rather limited arsenal.

The dev team over at Expression Games has taken that to heart. After addressing the two more glaring omissions by adding the American M14 and the Soviet SKS, the most iconic Western weapon of the Cold War is finally making its way to Southeast Asia.

The next major release for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, upgrade 2.0, is bringing the FN FAL into the fray, specifically in its British version that saw combat in the region.

Introduced in 1953, the FAL holds the distinction of being the first modern service rifle to enter widespread service in the West.

Chambered for the same 7.62x51mm NATO as the M14, M40 and M60 already in the game, the L1A1 SLR (Self-Loading Rifle) variant comes with a 20-round box magazine and is limited to semi-automatic fire. This was a design choice by Commonwealth clients, and really, unless you want to shoot down NVA planes while aiming at the horizon, you won’t notice the difference.

According to recent reports, in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, the L1A1 will be available to the United States & Allies faction to represent its service with Australian and Upcoming Zealander units deployed there. Unlike the M14, the new rifle won’t be available to the Rifleman role.

The FAL holds the distinction of being the first modern service rifle to enter widespread service in the West.

To use the L1A1, you’ll need to reach level 6 in one of the following roles:.

I want to caveat here that if you actually pick the L1A1 over the M60 while playing machine gunner, you are a bad person and your team will be short in firepower. MG roles are for pouring it on downrange, not for reloading after twenty shots, and I’m saying this as a staunch FAL defender.

The developers have not offered any insight on how the pilots are supposed to fit a rifle that long in the cockpit of the Huey, but we can look the other way for a little bit.

As much as I’m pining for the L1A1 and it will be my personal highlight of revision 2.0 for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, it’s hard to argue against the real massive item on the prospective patch notes being the Khe Sanh map and what it means for the game as a whole.

Khe Sanh will be the debut map for the Assault game mode, doubling down on the attackers versus defenders gameplay already present in the Offensive mode.

Sources indicate that assault brings back a fan favorite from the World War 2 Hell Let Loose, and focuses specifically on horrific trench warfare, strongpoints, and choosing whether you prefer dying in a fatal funnel in a trench or getting ripped apart by artillery out in the open. It’s great fun once you get used to the tinnitus.

Level designer Kienan Suthar provides more detail in this deep dive:.

The battle of Khe Sanh was one of the toughest battles in the Vietnam War, coinciding with the Tet Offensive of January 1968 and lasting until July of that same year.

Khe Sanh Combat Base was surrounded by a large North Vietnamese force, supported by Viet Cong and Pathet Lao rebels. For five months, US and allied forces reinforced the base primarily from the air, while throwing everything and the kitchen sink at the Vietnamese troops.

The outcome of the battle, as many major engagements of the Vietnam War, was inconclusive. The North Vietnamese siege was partially lifted by April 1968, but a shift in US strategy in the aftermath of the Tet Offensive led to its abandonment on July 9.

For the Americans, avoiding a Điện Biên Phủ situation and preventing the collapse of the base was considered a win. The North Vietnamese, meanwhile, celebrated victory by capturing the region following the withdrawal.

For players, the real tangible outcome is that it created an incredibly dense network of fortifications for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam to sink its teeth into the assault mode.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that loot boxes, dark patterns, virtual currencies, subscription services, pay-to-win systems, and many other trappings of diabolical digital serfdom all face extensive regulation under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has been formally presented to EU member states today.
  • It has been revealed that you can now read the draft text here on the EU Commission's official site.
  • Here's a summary from me, based on a quick delve through the text.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that loot boxes, dark patterns, virtual currencies, subscription services, pay-to-win systems, and many other trappings of diabolical digital serfdom all face extensive regulation under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has been formally presented to EU member states today. The full draft text of the regulation leaked earlier in the week. If it passes into law - and there's plenty of debate and revision ahead - it'll have massive consequences for the developers and publishers of games like Overwatch, Dota 2, and GTA Online.

It has been revealed that you can now read the draft text here on the EU Commission's official site. The organisers have also published an introductory explainer that takes us through the timeline of the Act's gestation, dating back to 2020, and summarises its provisions. If passed, the Act will apply to any company doing business in the EU, not just those based in member states, with individual governments able to impose fines and consumers able to seek financial compensation if they think they've been harmed.

Here's a summary from me, based on a quick delve through the text. The Act proposes a number of provisions regarding "unfair" commercial practices, including omission and distortion in advertising and PR communication at large. Amongst other things, it takes aim at "dark patterns" – that is, "visual, auditory and other components" of online interfaces that are designed to manipulate or deceive. The text also forbids personalised advertising and pricing aimed at children, and prohibits influencers from making "direct exhortations to minors to buy products or to persuade their parents or other adults to buy products in commercial communications".

The items that are probably of greatest interest to us smelly gamers are the passages on virtual currencies, "variable reward systems", and addictive design.

The Act would require game publishers who sell virtual currencies to indicate the real-world monetary value of the currency and anything bought with it. It would also require companies to disable paid-for virtual currencies by default for kids, unless a parent or guardian has given approval.

According to recent reports, as for paid-for "variable reward systems", aka "loot boxes", "surprise mechanics", "Schrödinger's Giftbombs" or however publishers may prefer to describe them, the Act would require companies to state the "types" of object they might cough up, together with the probability of obtaining them. It would also oblige publishers to disable paid-for "variable reward systems" for minors, and give everybody an "easily accessible" way to switch them off.

Recent findings suggest that the draft Act outright prohibits "pay-to-progress and pay-to-win mechanisms" for kids. More generally, it suggests further constraints for publishers and developers who "design, organise or operate their digital products in a manner that is intended, or can reasonably be foreseen to encourage compulsive or excessive use". Again, it wants companies to give people options to switch these features off.

That includes "features enabling automatic play of content and uninterrupted content consumption without effective and regular interruption moments that enable deliberation by the consumer on their willingness to consume more content". Also, "notifications not triggered by, or not directly related to, the consumer’s interaction or activity on the service", "features incentivising engagement at regular times or with greater frequency, including through penalties or loss of benefits", and "features and system behaviours that encourage continued use by simulating interpersonal relations," such as nagging prompts.

If you'd like a more 'expert' account of the Digital Fairness Act - how dare you! I have read several Wikipedia pages - the bespectacled nabobs of GamesIndustry.biz went and got notes from an actual lawyer. All this follows a change in EU rating law last month aimed at safeguarding the weans from predatory habit-forming devices and instruments of financialisation - games with lootboxes are now PEGI 16 by default, while blockchain games are always rated 18. Across the pond, meanwhile, lawsuits are underway in Upcoming York and Washington against Valve's tolerance of lootboxes on Steam, which the lawyers in question define as illegal gambling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being. Across its history, there's only ever been one GTA game set outside America: the London-based expansion of the original game.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami. But what about the next game - will the series always be in America? Not necessarily.

In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then swiftly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".

According to recent reports, this is a topic Rockstar has responded to before, most notably when firm co-founder and long-time GTA writer Dan Houser - who's no longer at Rockstar - discussed why the series always seemed to return to America. He mentioned it was because cities like Miami and New York and Los Angeles are places where extreme juxtapositions exist. They're places where extreme wealth rubs shoulders with extreme poverty, and where organised crime can be found.

There's also something America infamously has that few other countries do, and that's free availability of guns, which is such a core tenet of a GTA experience.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, Obbe Vermeij - a former technical director at Rockstar North - revealed last year that a GTA: Tokyo almost happened. However, it wasn't going to be made by Rockstar but rather an external team in Japan.

While discussing the subject, Vermeij referred to America as "basically the epicenter of Western culture". "Everybody knows the cities, even people who haven't been there," Vermeij mentioned. "They have a mental image of the cities. I'm afraid we're stuck in this loop of about five American cities. Let's just get used to it.".

GTA 6 is just days away from its 19th November release on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar recently clarified the game runs at 30FPS across all platforms and confirmed that while it's available through Xbox Cloud Gaming, it cannot be streamed to PCs or non-Xbox devices.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that black Forest Games, developers of the Destroy All Humans!
  • It has been revealed that black Forest, based in Germany, declared the move in a press release.
  • "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred," added Third Signal founder Andreas Tobler.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that black Forest Games, developers of the Destroy All Humans! remakes, have spun out of Embracer Group-owned publishers THQ Nordic via a management buyout and announced prepares to form a upcoming "developer-driven group" of independent studios. The new group, dubbed Third Signal, will aim to "give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom" to "bring their own ideas to life".

It has been revealed that black Forest, based in Germany, declared the move in a press release. "We are grateful to THQ Nordic and Embracer for nine good years and the games we made together," co-boss Adrian Goersch remarked. "Now, we're excited to shape our own future as owners again, to work on an exciting newly introduced project with a great team and strong partners behind us.".

"Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred," added Third Signal founder Andreas Tobler. "Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life." As of writing, Third Signal's website is just a logo splash which promises something coming soon. To be fair, it does also look to have an email address, plus legal and privacy notices. Black Forest's management team will become a co-owner of the studio group as part of this move, but "continue to collaborate on game development tasks" with THQ Nordic.

According to recent reports, black Forest had been in the embrace since 2017, releasing both 2020's Destroy All Humans! remake and Destroy All Humans! 2: Reprobed in that time, plus DLC Clone Carnage. Over the years they've also made multiple entries in the Giana Sisters platformer series, survival game Fade to Silence, and 2017's Bubsy: The Woolies Strike Back.

That's a right old mix of stuff, but the biggest names in it are all resurrections of series or characters created by other folks back in the day. Pandemic Studios in the case of Destroy All Humans!, Accolade in the case of Bubsy, and Germany organization Time Warp in the case of Giana Sisters. That makes the fact it sounds like this move'll give Black Forest a bit more creative freedom intriguing. Here's hoping that if they do plan to try and get some more of their own original ideas off the ground, rather than trucking on with a steady diet of remakes and revivals, they manage to stick the landing. It's all fine declaring that a 50 person team can make a top game these days, but that certainly doesn't mean it's in any way easy to pull off.

10 Games to Play If You Loved Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there are few things worse than finishing a fantastic adventure and realizing you have no idea what to play next.
  • After spending hours exploring Hyrule, solving puzzles, and facing some of gaming's most memorable bosses, it's only natural to feel a little lost when the credits finally roll.
  • While no game can truly replace the feeling of playing Ocarina of Time for the first time, there are plenty of experiences out there that capture some of the same magic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there are few things worse than finishing a fantastic adventure and realizing you have no idea what to play next. With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake arriving earlier this month, plenty of players are probably reaching that bittersweet moment already!

After spending hours exploring Hyrule, solving puzzles, and facing some of gaming's most memorable bosses, it's only natural to feel a little lost when the credits finally roll. But don't worry, because I'm here to help you find your next adventure.

While no game can truly replace the feeling of playing Ocarina of Time for the first time, there are plenty of experiences out there that capture some of the same magic. Whether it's a mysterious world waiting to be explored, clever dungeons, unforgettable characters, or a story that stays with you long after you've put the controller down, there's something on this list for every kind of Zelda fan.

Recent findings suggest that so, if you're already missing Hyrule and aren't quite ready to say goodbye to that feeling of adventure, here are 10 games worth checking out. Some might remind you of classic Zelda, while others take those familiar ideas in completely different directions. Either way, I think you'll find something worth getting lost in!

According to recent reports, nothing beats dealing with the sadness of finishing a fantastic game by jumping straight into its sequel, right? That's why we're kicking things off with Majora's Mask, the final Zelda entry released on the Nintendo 64 and one of the darkest adventures in the entire franchise.

Industry observers note that although it reuses plenty of assets and the basic gameplay of Ocarina of Time, Majora's has an entirely different atmosphere. There's no Triforce, no Princess Zelda to rescue, and no Ganondorf plotting to take over Hyrule. Instead, a mysterious moon is about to crash into the town of Termina, and Link happens to have his Ocarina stolen by the mischievous creature responsible for the whole mess – then, well, someone has to save the day!

Recent findings suggest that this leads to one of the most fascinating mechanics in the series: a three-day time loop that has you traveling through time, helping eccentric characters, and learning the daily schedules of the town's residents. Interestingly, the Ocarina of Time remake actually brings a little more of that NPC schedule system into its own villages, making this sequel feel like a particularly natural follow-up.

If you love the combination of dungeons, memorable boss fights, unusual mechanics, and, of course, a lovely talking companion, then Okami should be right up your alley.

Sources indicate that with a structure heavily inspired by classic Zelda adventures, this is one of Capcom's most beloved games, and its story draws heavily from Japanese folklore, following Amaterasu, the sun goddess who takes the form of a white wolf. She must restore life to a land plagued by an ancient evil, beginning with a legendary eight-headed demon that was sealed away a hundred years earlier. Gods, broken seals, spirits, and a spreading darkness? Yeah, I think that should ring a bell for anyone familiar with Hyrule.

It's a perfect pick if you're craving another Zelda-like adventure, and the upcoming sequel gives you one more reason to fall in love with this world.

In a recent development, mina the Hollower takes place in a world filled with talking skeletons and every kind of magical fantasy you can imagine. So, if the Ocarina of Time left you craving another adventure packed with charming characters and a wonderfully imaginative world, this little indie game might be exactly what you're looking for.

This is a 2D action-adventure with roots deeply tied to some of the most iconic games in the genre – and yes, The Legend of Zelda is definitely one of its biggest inspirations. Between its top-down perspective, exploration, combat, and dungeon-like challenges, you'll probably catch some familiar vibes from the original Zelda and A Link to the Past along the way.

Industry observers note that what I particularly love, though, is how Mina the Hollower manages to feel like a love letter to those classics without simply copying them. Its unique story and charming gothic aesthetic give it an identity of its own.

If one of the things that stayed with you after playing Ocarina of Time was its bittersweet take on growing up and letting go of the past, then Shadow of the Colossus is an excellent next stop.

This is a much quieter and more melancholic adventure, but it shares that ability to make you feel like you're part of something much bigger than yourself. Instead of exploring villages and dungeons, you'll travel across an enormous, almost deserted landscape on horseback, searching for sixteen colossal creatures. And each encounter is essentially a puzzle of its own, requiring you to figure out how to climb these mysterious beings and find their weak points before delivering the final blow.

And trust me, there's something incredibly special about the atmosphere here! Much like Zelda, the world invites you to explore and take in its surroundings, but there's a sadness lingering beneath all that beauty. If you're looking for another adventure that makes you stop and think about the things we leave behind, this one is hard to beat.

According to recent reports, I mean, just look at Tunic’s cover! Do I need to say more? Jokes aside, this lovely indie adventure is another love letter to classic Zelda titles, and what I love most about it is how it perfectly understands the feeling of trusting players to let them figure things out for themselves.

It has been revealed that so if you loved the sense of discovery in Ocarina of Time, you're going to feel right at home here! Besides, you play as a little fox exploring a beautifully crafted world filled with hidden passages, dangerous enemies, challenging bosses, and secrets that often require a second look.

Recent findings suggest that also, Tunic makes exploration feel rewarding in a way that goes beyond simply finding another collectible. Even the game's instruction manual becomes part of the adventure, encouraging you to piece together its mysteries as you go! It's a lovely reminder of why discovering something on your own can be so much more exciting than having the game explain it to you.

If you're still craving that classic Zelda combination of dungeons, clever puzzles, memorable boss fights, and ingenious equipment, Death's Door deserves a spot on your list. It's another indie adventure with a strong love for the genre, but it manages to give those familiar ingredients a personality of its own.

You play as a little crow working as a reaper, collecting souls in a strange world where death has become an increasingly complicated business. Along the way, you'll explore interconnected areas and face some genuinely challenging enemies. The combat is also fast and satisfying, while its dungeons offer plenty of clever environmental puzzles.

What really brings everything together, though, is the atmosphere. The world is wonderfully quirky, the soundtrack is fantastic, and there's a surprising amount of heart beneath its dark humor. It might not be Hyrule, but I think any Zelda fan looking for another compact adventure full of secrets and memorable encounters will have a great time here.

Sometimes, all you need after finishing a Zelda title is another gorgeous fantasy world to get lost in. And that's exactly what Kena: Bridge of Spirits offers. Its colorful environments and charming characters almost look like they've been pulled straight out of an animated movie, making it an easy recommendation if you loved the magical atmosphere of Ocarina of Time.

Industry observers note that but don't let the adorable presentation fool you, though. Kena's combat can get surprisingly challenging, especially when you face some of its larger bosses! Around here, you play as a spirit guide traveling through a beautiful but corrupted land, helping lost souls move on while uncovering the story behind the world around her.

Recent findings suggest that this means that exploration is a big part of the experience, with environmental puzzles and little companions called Rot helping you interact with your surroundings. So there’s a little bit of everything, and it is quite easy to get lost in it!

Sure, most titles on this list are modern games because they're more accessible, but I remember that, back in the day, when I got the post-Ocarina of Time blues, it was Banjo-Tooie that saved me from the heartbreak.

Developed by Rare, this classic platformer takes the colorful gameplay of its predecessor (although you don't need to play the first game to enjoy this one) and expands it into a much bigger experience, with enormous interconnected worlds and plenty of secrets to uncover. There's just a lot to discover in each area, and the way different worlds connect makes exploration particularly rewarding.

Sources indicate that it's obviously a different kind of adventure from Zelda, leaning more heavily into 3D platforming, but there's something very familiar about the joy of exploring every corner of its environments. Plus, Banjo-Tooie has plenty of that same old-school magic.

It has been revealed that one of the things I love most about Zelda is how its adventures can feel both fantastical and surprisingly emotional. If you're looking for another series that combines an imaginative world with a story about friendship, destiny, and growing up, Kingdom Hearts is definitely worth your time.

According to recent reports, and the 1.5 + 2.5 ReMIX collection is a great way to experience several important entries in the series and completely immerse yourself in this universe. Okay, maybe I'm cheating a little here, but we're in the middle of a new GTA era, so let me have this one!

Of course, I should also warn you that Kingdom Hearts has a much more confusing story than your average Zelda adventure. But underneath all those twists and mysterious characters is a genuinely heartfelt journey about the bonds we create and the people we want to protect.

Okay, hear me out: even though Metroid Prime Remastered is a first-person sci-fi adventure, it has more in common with Zelda than you might initially expect. In fact, its exploration structure is practically built around the same kind of progression that makes classic Zelda games so satisfying! If you loved finding a new item in Ocarina of Time and immediately wondering which previously inaccessible areas you could now explore, you'll understand what I mean.

Playing as Samus Aran, you'll explore the interconnected regions of the planet Tallon IV, scanning your surroundings and uncovering the mysteries of an ancient civilization. As you acquire newly introduced upgrades and abilities, paths that were previously blocked suddenly become accessible, encouraging you to revisit familiar locations with a fresh perspective.

The biggest difference is that you're doing all of this through a first-person perspective, with a much stronger emphasis on shooting and atmospheric exploration. But the satisfaction of gradually understanding how the world fits together is pure Zelda – a lovely reminder that a great adventure doesn't need to take place in Hyrule to capture that same magic.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the organization.
  • It has been revealed that in a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox noted Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the tech giant's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027.
  • Sources indicate that "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester noted of his decision.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the organization. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

It has been revealed that in a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox noted Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the tech giant's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

Sources indicate that "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester noted of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My proposal was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the tech giant's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level.".

Industry observers note that wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the manufacturer in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally rolled out last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox announced a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

Wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a upcoming studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

Despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus.".

According to recent reports, paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.

Whenever I mention that I write about mobile gaming, the inevitable first response from laymen and industry people alike is, 'Well, that's all just gacha, right?' And on the one hand, they're not necessarily right, but not wrong either. The random draw system is so pervasive that even many developers pit themselves against it, like with the upcoming Mixcity Swap.

It has been revealed that positioning itself as the anti-gacha, Mixcity Swap is an upcoming sports-themed card battler by Atypique Studio, releasing in 2027 for iOS and Android, that sees you taking on fast-paced, 10-minute matches. With only nine cards on the roster, the gameplay revolves around swapping in and out your athletes across different modes, doing so at the right interval as they activate their individual effects.

It has been revealed that in that way, I think positing it as anti gacha is a bit of a misnomer. At its core, Mixcity Swap looks to be an exciting standalone card game, and one that doesn't really need to pit itself against such a widely reviled mechanic to be successful.

But, I'll certainly be interested to see how Atypique prepares to grow this game in future. We've got plenty of small-scale card battlers that avoid gacha, but a long-term live-service type release may be a very different beast to keep loyal to that ideal.

Sources indicate that still, if you find yourself wanting more card-battling action on mobile, then you're not without plenty of options to try. Just take a look at our list of the best card battlers on iOS, and you'll find some choice picks you can play right now!

#75180. Latest Update: There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1906 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price.
  • In a recent development, in 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves.
  • But the Nvidia of the late 1990s and early 2000s was a far cry from the vast (if tarnished) juggernaut it is today, and at the time it wasn’t even the obvious survivor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price. It was choosing the right one among a glut of potential, reasonably affordable options.

In a recent development, in 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves. Just two years later, at the turn of the latest millennium, only 15 remained, and not long after that, there were merely two: Nvidia and ATI, nowadays part of AMD.

But the Nvidia of the late 1990s and early 2000s was a far cry from the vast (if tarnished) juggernaut it is today, and at the time it wasn’t even the obvious survivor. Research firm 4th Wave put ATI top for 1998 with 24.5 million 3D chips sold, followed by S3 with 15.2 million and Intel, in its first year in the market, with 6.5 million. Nvidia came fourth on 6.4 million. 3dfx, the organization whose Voodoo cards had made 3D gaming on PC a thing in the first place, sold 5.2 million.

Recent findings suggest that each of those companies went under or sold up for one reason or another, but what’s striking is how most did so within a few years of one another. In the four years between 1998 and 2002, the graphics business essentially stopped rewarding whoever had the fastest chip, instead favouring the companies that could iterate the fastest. A new chip every six months or so for the same APIs everyone used, backed by enough capital to ride out the dot-com crash. Nvidia was built for that; almost nobody else was.

The first companies to go didn’t need any help from Nvidia, though. 3D acceleration had made the humble graphics chip a much bigger and more expensive thing to design, and plenty of incumbents that had found their footing on 2D couldn’t afford to keep going. Tseng Labs stopped developing graphics chips at the end of 1997 with roughly $28 million still in the bank, selling its graphics engineers to ATI for about $3 million. Rendition, maker of the Vérité V1000 3D accelerator, agreed to sell itself to memory maker Micron in June 1998, and ATI bought Chromatic Research for $67 million that October.

In its prospectus for its January 1999 IPO, Nvidia warned that PC makers brought out latest systems as often as twice a year, on a spring and fall schedule, and that missing one was a serious risk. The organization subsequently reorganised itself around that schedule, releasing the GeForce 256 in October 1999 and the GeForce 3 in February 2001. By 2002, Nvidia’s annual report disclosed that separate design teams were working on several generations of chips at once.

By this point, though, the writing had been on the wall for quite some time. S3, then the world’s second-largest graphics chip maker, wrote in its annual report for 1999 that a graphics chip stayed on sale for 12 to 18 months, and that a delay "as short as a few months" could cost it a design win with a PC maker. Any company that was rolling out just one major chip per year was launching against a rival’s refresh at best. At worst, it was launching late against next-gen chips.

That’s essentially what happened to 3dfx when Rampage, the chip that was meant to succeed the Voodoo5, never shipped. The firm lost its other major advantage around the same time with Glide, its own programming interface that only ran on Voodoo cards. Glide flourished while Direct3D, Microsoft’s rival interface built into Windows, was still lacking features, meaning that plenty of games ran best on 3dfx hardware, but that lead was swiftly eroded once Direct3D and rivals’ OpenGL drivers caught up; developers could now write a game once and run it on anyone’s card. By 1999, Creative was selling Nvidia-based Riva TNT cards with drivers that let Glide games run on them. 3dfx sued, then open-sourced Glide altogether that December.

By then, though, 3dfx had already made its most damaging mistake. A year earlier, on December 14, 1998, it agreed to buy graphics card maker STB Systems for about $141 million in stock, and CEO Greg Ballard remarked the Voodoo3 would only be sold on 3dfx’s cards. That revelation left Diamond and Creative in a tough spot, having built their gaming lines on Voodoo chips. They were now stuck high and dry without access to the new one.

3dfx was solely concerned with its margins here. The price of its single-chip Voodoo Banshee card dropped from $150 to $89 within a month of launch. With prices in freefall, selling the finished Voodoo Banshee meant that 3dfx pocketed the margin that’d otherwise go to a partner like Diamond or Creative. Those boardmakers inevitably walked, and went where the chips were. STB had been selling Nvidia cards right up to the deal, and its last annual report includes a $3 million note it held from "Nvidia Corporation, a supplier." Creative already had Riva TNT cards on shelves, and Nvidia, which then didn’t make its own cards, would sell its chips to anyone.

According to recent reports, intel, meanwhile, was causing problems from the other end of the market. Its i740 "Auburn" graphics chip launched in early 1998, and Microprocessor Report, the newsletter for the industry’s engineers, argued that Intel’s arrival encouraged Cirrus Logic, Oak and others to fold that year. Just over a year later, after lacklustre sales, Intel confirmed that it was ending support for the i740, then pulled out of standalone desktop graphics chips altogether to put graphics into its motherboard chipsets instead, starting with the i810. This was extremely problematic for companies like S3, Trident, and SiS. They survived on cheap chips for massive PC makers, and by the second half of 2001, estimates say Intel’s integrated graphics business had risen to control 55% of the market. That, in turn, pushed S3 to sell its graphics business to a VIA joint venture for $323 million.

Industry observers note that then the money ran out. Venture funding for graphics startups had already dried up in 1999 as the dot-com bubble deflated, and exits inevitably followed. 3dfx lost $100.5 million in the second quarter of 2000, with its CEO blaming a late Voodoo5, and on December 15 that year it sold its assets to Nvidia for $70 million in cash (and a million Nvidia shares) after failing to secure credit. STMicroelectronics, which made the PowerVR-based Kyro II, quit PC graphics in early 2002.

Recent findings suggest that ATI, however, survived alongside Nvidia because it was already operating in the way the upcoming market wanted it to. It was the biggest seller at the time, and it made its own graphics cards, which Microprocessor Report noted brought in most of its revenue and margin. So, making its own cards wasn’t 3dfx’s mistake; it was locking out boardmakers who had been selling Voodoo cards for it. That pushed those boardmakers towards Nvidia, and a late Voodoo5 and cash crunch dealt the death blow. ATI also used its stock to buy the engineers that its rivals were shedding: Tseng’s, Chromatic’s, then, in February 2000, ArtX’s for $400 million, a team that’d just designed the Flipper graphics chip for Nintendo’s GameCube.

Recent findings suggest that for the next two decades, the the graphics industry was dominated by ATI - which eventually folded into AMD in 2006 - and Nvidia. For a while, it was a real fight. AMD paid $5.4 billion for ATI, and in the second quarter of 2010, Radeon cards briefly overtook Nvidia in discrete graphics shipments. However, AMD had a problem: it couldn’t really afford ATI. It wrote off $1.6 billion of goodwill from the deal about a year after it closed, and its PC chip business kept struggling.

Industry observers note that by early 2015, AMD’s CPU and GPU revenue was down 38% on the year, and the firm was close to negative book value. Its quarterly R&D budget had fallen to its lowest level since 2004, with Nvidia spending nearly half as much again. Radeon cards stayed on the same Graphics Core Next architecture for about seven years before RDNA arrived in 2019. By then, Nvidia had already introduced its RTX cards with dedicated ray tracing hardware and Tensor cores for AI, and it never gave that lead back.

Intel was the only tech giant with pockets deep enough to try breaking back in. Its first go, Larrabee, was cancelled as a consumer graphics chip in December 2009. It finally got there in 2022, when the Arc A770 went on sale from $329, alongside the cheaper A750. Both arrived after repeated delays and struggled with older DirectX 9 games, and many observers - RPS included - put their chances of breaking up the Nvidia-AMD duopoly at low. By the time then-hardware editor James returned to the A750 in 2023, Intel had drastically improved its drivers, bringing significant gains to both general performance and DX9 compatibility. Even then, the Arc series had yet to prove it could work well at launch, without the need to be ironed out across months of updates.

In a recent development, the second generation did indeed fare better, with the Arc B580 successfully selling out at $249 in December 2024. But that still barely impacted the wider industry, with Intel sitting at just 1% of graphics card shipments in the third quarter of 2025 and around 2% this spring, when Nvidia took roughly 90% of the 12.5 million cards shipped.

It now looks like Intel is on its way back out of gaming graphics cards. In April, leaker Jaykihn claimed that its next-generation Celestial gaming cards had been cancelled "long ago," and the latest rumours say B580 supply could be cut so Intel can sell more Arc Pro cards for, surprise surprise, AI work. It’s notable to note that Intel hasn’t confirmed any of that, and one of its execs has said that Arc isn’t leaving its PC roadmap. Still, Intel had everything 3dfx didn’t: the cash, the PC makers on side, and the same APIs as everyone else. But money can’t buy two decades of Nvidia and AMD fixing their drivers game by game, and it seems to have decided its capital is better spent on AI anyway.

Recent findings suggest that evidently, the question of where all the other GPU makers went does not have one single answer. Some couldn’t afford the rising costs, some couldn’t keep pace with a new Nvidia chip every six months, and some lost their cheap business to Intel’s integrated graphics or went under when the dot-com bubble burst. Left over was a Nvidia/ATI (later AMD) duopoly, and PC gamers haven’t exactly done well out of it. We saw the RTX 4080 launch at $1,199 in 2022, nearly twice the 3080’s price, and the ongoing, AI-driven RAM shortage has pushed prices higher still.

Sources indicate that in 1998, 47 companies wanted your money. Now there are two, and the bigger one, Nvidia, sells nine of every 10 graphics cards - yet still makes most of its money from data centres. Eighteen years on, it's a bad time to be a PC gamer, and nobody’s in a hurry to make things any better.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another substantial content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright.
  • If you couldn’t guess already, the new theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.
  • According to recent reports, the big new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another substantial content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the new theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

According to recent reports, the big new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

These are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

According to recent reports, the Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

The other substantial addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Sources indicate that chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a fresh Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

Sources indicate that as with every major enhancement, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To get into the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe in GTA 6, you can either obtain the safe code, which is far harder than it sounds, or you can blow it open, which is the much easier way to get in. If you'd still rather unlock the safe the classic way, I'll explain both methods of getting into the safe below, including how to get the GTA 6 bowling alley safe code. Whichever road you go down, it'll help you save up some cash and get back on your feet - and take down a few of those pesky Kolt gang members while you're at it.

According to recent reports, the GTA 6 Bowling Alley safe code is 0300. To find it for yourself, you need to go to Brooks Boatworks, as hinted at in the notepad next to the safe. The safe code is on a map on the wall in one of the buildings there, as marked on the image above.

Recent findings suggest that by the time the bowling alley is mentioned, Brooks Boatworks should be marked on your map as another location held by the Kolt crew, and you may have even raided it already. Whether you've been there or not, the map is found on the wall of an office in the raised buildings to the east of the area, and you can find two other GTA 6 safe codes on this map, too.

Sources indicate that you'll have to fend off a lot of Kolt members at both the bowling alley and the boatworks, so make sure you've got some decent GTA 6 guns to hand, and certainly as much Zombix as you can carry. You'll find more at each location, too, so keep an eye out.

You'll also see the option to plant explosives on the GTA 6 bowling alley safe, but if you haven't got the right explosives to hand, the option is grayed out. Fortunately, there are some sticky bombs conveniently stashed in the next room, meaning it's the much safer option that heading out to the boatworks.

We previously believed this option required reaching one of the Chapter 3 GTA 6 missions, at which point you unlock the ability to buy sticky bombs from Ammu-Nation, but with the few explosives available in the bowling alley, you're golden. Keep the spares on you, and you can use them to get into other safes around Leonida, too.

Shopify Rebellion Black opened the North America Qualifier Playoffs with a 2-0 win over Xora Esports. The non-partner organisation is now one win from the playoffs that decide a guaranteed São Paulo Kickoff place.

The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.

It has been revealed that the result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system. The organisation was one of the Americas sides that said it had not been chosen for the 2027-2028 partnership programme, Sheep Esports reported. Cloud9, ENVY, M80, FlyQuest and LYON were also on that list. Riot now has eight partner teams in each of its four regions.

Sources indicate that the Swiss Stage runs from 20 to 22 November 2026. Every match is best of three. Two wins send a team through to the playoffs, and two losses knock it out. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

In a recent development, shopify Rebellion Black’s next opponents are Oafs, who also won their opening match 2-0, against QoR. Both teams are therefore one win from the playoffs. Oafs already have a record against Xora. They knocked them out of the Qualifier 1 bracket on 8 November with a 2-1 win. Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

Recent findings suggest that across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

Sources indicate that the organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

Recent findings suggest that the prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Developer FromSoftware has announced that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.

According to recent reports, fromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server problem". Some speculated this could be related to the recently discovered PHP security bug, which impacted a number of other games.

FromSoftware never specified the exact issue impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague. "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2, and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored," a notice on Dark Souls' official site reads.

"We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding.".

Online servers do more in FromSoftware games than simply facilitating co-op and PvP; they're also responsible for handling messages players leave for each other in-game, as well as the ghostly representations of players who just went through the same area, helping the Dark Souls series' forlorn worlds feel a little less solitary.

According to recent reports, this isn't the first time Dark Souls servers have gone offline, either. In 2022, servers for all three games went offline due to a vulnerability that allowed malicious code to run on them. In that instance, it took FromSoftware three months to bring servers back online for some games, and as many as nine months for others.

In other FromSoftware news, the studio recently announced - following months of speculation - it's officially delaying the Switch 2-exclusive The Duskbloods to sometime in 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, using cheats in GTA 6 is a given.
  • Recent findings suggest that naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats.
  • Maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, using cheats in GTA 6 is a given. GTA games are substantial, beautiful sandboxes of destruction, and sometimes I want to forget about story missions and just magically fill my pockets with cash, spawn a tank or a jet, and go on a rampage with infinite incendiary ammo.

Recent findings suggest that naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats. But only eventually. If you were hoping to try out some cheats the moment you step into the game, I've got some bad news for you—and then some worse news. Here are the problems:.

Maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting. But then again, if you shell out potentially $100 for a game, shouldn't you be able to play it however the heck you want? I think so.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 is a big, long game, with a five chapter main story that contains 91 missions. It took me about 90 hours to finish, at which point I could finally access the cheats menu.

That's where I found the next bit of bad news...

Congrats on playing those 90 hours: are you ready for 90 more? Most cheats on the menu are locked because there are requirements you need to meet to use them. Want a cheat that removes fall damage? First you'll need to survive 20 falls of over more than 40 feet. Want to spawn a parachute? First complete 50 skydives and basejumps.

Recent findings suggest that using an infinite ammo cheat means first winning 25 medals on shooting ranges. To fast-forward time you'll need to find 10 collectible watches—and in 90 hours I found exactly one of them. Spawning a jet means first completing every single challenge in the game, which is gonna take, ooh, let me check… forever.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

I don't love this cheat unlock system at all, but there's even more bad news:.

Want to use a cheat to give yourself an extra $250,000 so you can go on a car buying spree? Cool, go ahead. But you won't be able to save your progress once you enable a cheat.

Recent findings suggest that whatever fun you have cheating is purely of the sandbox variety. You can buy cars and clothes and guns with cheated money, but you'll lose it all when you stop playing because you're not allowed to save your game once you use a single cheat. Booo.

And there's one final bummer for ya:.

I tried it. I opened an older save where I hadn't yet completed the main story, and tried to input the cheats I'd learned from my complete game save. No dice! The cheats don't work unless you're using a save file that's story complete. So, starting over at the beginning and using cheats? Not gonna happen.

Industry observers note that I'm really not a fan of this. With so many restrictions in place, Rockstar has really taken the fun out of being a huge GTA cheater! When GTA 6 finally comes to PC, I hope modders make cheats their top priority.

Hello! And welcome back to The Wrapp, where we natter about our weekend gaming prepares for a bit. This time, Catherine's taken up stamping passports as a profession while Iwan's struggling to get words down. Elsewhere, Dann and I are puzzled by the colour brown while Shaun's off being a sky pirate.

Recent findings suggest that sadly, I have been pulled back into Neopets Faerie Fragments due to them running a Neopets.com event that had a battle pass, and one way to get points in the battle pass is to play Neopets Faerie Fragments. I am happy to report that the daily runs, which challenge you to do a string of levels one after another, are far easier than where I am in the main questline! There’s also a sub-questline that doesn’t give you coins (only clothing coins?!) in a very glitched and black world, that I also was able to play through, so I have been knocking those out each day.

In a recent development, I’m still trying my hardest to survive Warhammer Survivors, but something else has actually caught my eye this week - and that’s Lil’ Guardsman on mobile, simply because the art style reminds me so much of Lost in Play. I’m prone to judging games by their proverbial cover, so I have a feeling I’ll enjoy this fantasy take on border patrol very, very much.

Right, time to throw these pesky humans to the dungeons (insert Lemongrab-inspired screeching here)!

Recent findings suggest that the game world is being affected this week in so many ways, some of which we have discussed, but how will it affect us? Well, multiple mobile games were released recently, and more are opting for the 'buy before you try' system. As long as they're clear about it, I think it's a pretty effective way to give folks a solid taste of something.

In a recent development, one such game that has been blatant about it on booting it up is Booster Pack: Heroes. I like opening cards, I like cool characters, and I like RPG elements, so this seems right up my alley… But it's only got an hour to get through it.

In a recent development, this month I’ve been trying my best to accomplish National Novel Writing Month. Even with the organisation being defunct, the challenge remains. But sadly, I think it’s defeated me, as 1667 words a day is surprisingly difficult if you want to, you know, have a life outside work.

Industry observers note that that doesn’t mean I’m about to stop writing, though, and I’ll be working on plenty of stuff this weekend. As well as digging into an interesting fresh visual novel, featuring vampires, emotional therapy and some rather flashy clothes. Can’t guess what? You’ll have to wait to find out!

In a recent development, I’m always quite excited to see a new Bart Bonte game hitting mobile. While brown certainly might not be the most appealing colour, I’m very excited to jump into his next entry in the colour series… It feels like it’s been a particularly long time since the last outing, so it’s a welcome return.

Industry observers note that yesterday I decided to pick up Warhammer Survivors, following the clamour from my co-workers last week. And I have to say, it is unfortunately a bit rubbish. You feel so sluggish and slow, plodding along, and if you pick a character with a Boltgun, good luck killing the weakest enemies in 3 hits. Even when you are fully decked out with the best gun and chainsword, it still feels like you are aimlessly wandering around.

Of course, though, we can’t just ignore the massive release this week. It is what we have all been waiting for; Spirit Crossing is out of Netflix exclusivity and available on iOS. I don’t know that much about it beyond it being MMO-ish, but the launch trailer highlights an airship turned into a house. So, I shall be an air pirate! The closest to a modern Skies of Arcadia Legends we will apparently get.

Much like Dann, I'm happy to see Bart Bonte is back on his colours. While Leaving Home and Mister Antonio are great, they don't hit the same way Pink, Red, Orange, and so on do. They remind me of the old Flash favourite, The Impossible Quiz, which I used to love. It's like a healthy dose of nostalgia with completely newly introduced ideas.
