💡 Key Takeaways
  • HoYoverse just wrapped up a significant Honkai: Star Rail Special Program.
  • Industry observers note that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
  • According to recent reports, planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a significant Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

Industry observers note that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the substantial latest world headlining Version 4.0.

According to recent reports, planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

According to recent reports, as you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Industry observers note that version 4.0 introduces two upcoming 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

According to recent reports, her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

It has been revealed that the other upcoming arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

According to recent reports, when you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

In a recent development, she also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Sources indicate that version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the fresh outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

Industry observers note that if you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that during your Grand Theft Auto 6 playthrough, you will eventually get the opportunity to register a car.
  • Sources indicate that this opportunity comes at the start of Chapter 2, where you learn about a man named Moses who deals with stolen cars.
  • Recent findings suggest that instead of stealing the coolest car to register, I recommend going a different route.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that during your Grand Theft Auto 6 playthrough, you will eventually get the opportunity to register a car. Registering cars allows you to call them easily from your phone with a small BuckMe fee.

Sources indicate that this opportunity comes at the start of Chapter 2, where you learn about a man named Moses who deals with stolen cars. To unlock Moses and his shop for good, you need to bring him your very first car to register.

Recent findings suggest that instead of stealing the coolest car to register, I recommend going a different route. Here’s the best starter car to register in GTA 6.

During the first mission of Chapter 2 in GTA 6, you will naturally meet a girl named Vicki. During this mission, Vicki will eventually mention Moses to Lucia, and once she does, Moses shop will be marked on the map with the objective to bring him a starter car to register.

After bringing Moses one car and registering it with him for free, you will unlock the ability to register most cars in Leonida. The only cars you can’t register with Moses are the ones with trackers, so make a mental note of that.

Also, keep in mind that even though you can register your starter car for free, registering every other car from here on out will cost you money. The price of registration depends on the type of car.

While players may want to steal and register the flashiest car in Leonida as their starter, this isn’t necessarily the smartest move. The nice sports cars won’t have the most trunk space and can be hard to control.

Instead, it would be best to choose a pickup truck for a starter car, as they have a ton of stash space and are generally easy to drive.

Recent findings suggest that it may seem unimportant, but having more stash space will allow Lucia to transport more money and robbery loot on a single trip. This means you can gather money faster, without constantly needing to visit ATMs.

Additionally, as previously mentioned, pickup trucks are generally on the easier side to control when driving. This is vital early in the game since it will allow you to have an easier time exploring, crashing less, and avoiding the need to pay for repairs.

Once you've built up wealth by using your starter car as a getaway and stash for loot from robberies and muggings, you can use any extra cash to register nicer vehicles.

Simply put, the coolest cars tend to have the highest registration price, so you want a reliable one that will help you get around easier and stash more money to start off.

According to recent reports, while there are many pickup trucks to find across the map of GTA VI, I have had the best luck finding them in parking lots. More specifically, I have found pickup trucks commonly in parking lots in front of bars, clothing shops, barbershops, etc.

In other words, pickup trucks are very easy to find, considering they aren’t that special when it comes to style and speed and aren’t considered “rare.” If you are worried about finding one in a specific color, you shouldn’t be, considering Moses makes you change the color when you bring it in.

Once you find a pickup truck (or a different car if you decided not to listen to my advice), bring it on over to Moses and tell him you’d like to register it.

After the quick transaction with Moses is complete, you are now able to call your starter car to your location whenever you like for a small BuckMe price via the Scooter Bros app on your phone.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, world of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch.
  • It has been revealed that but it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D.
  • Sources indicate that world of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, world of Warcraft: Forever players are having a blast in the new MMO, but not everyone is basking in the rays of its successful launch. Players located in Australia, New Zealand, and other Oceania countries are having a bit of a sunlight problem.

It has been revealed that but it's not that too much time behind the computer is keeping WoW players on the other side of the globe away from their precious Vitamin D. Rather, it's in-game sunlight that's scarce for our Oceania friends.

Sources indicate that world of Warcraft: Forever, if you didn't already known, has a lovely in-game day/night cycle that aligns with your server clock rather than your local time. So, for a British player, the server time is one hour ahead of GMT. That means if I play during the day I see the sun hanging over Azeroth, and if I do a late night MMO session it's replaced by the moon.

Industry observers note that however, while Oceania players can access a data centre in Australia that allows for a solid connection to WoW, they still share the same mega-servers with North Americans. That mega-server is aligned with North American time, differing drastically from Oceania time zones. In other words, for World of Warcraft: Forever players in Oceania, day is night and night is day. And they've had enough!

Reddit user Playful_Artichoke981 has been at the forefront of requests asking Blizzard to address the problem , though they're far from alone. Presently, Oceania players see full daylight in-game from around midnight to 6am in the morning, which obviously is far from normal gaming hours for the majority of players in the region.

Industry observers note that "We don't hate the nighttime. We just want variety," writes Playful_Artichoke981. "We don't want to have to compromise our sleep schedules to experience this game in all its glory." Another user, cuddlegoop, echoes the sentiment: "I am totally fine with my day/night changing when I join an NA party. Just let me see the sun! I was up late last night and the view over the bay at Shadowfan Keep in the dawn was so beautiful I want to see stuff like that more often.".

Eurogamer has contacted Blizzard to ask if it has prepares to address the issue, but we've not received a response at the time of writing.

In a recent development, world of Warcraft: Forever is proving exceptionally popular, breaking records as the biggest launch in the series' history. And based on what I've played this week, it's looking to be a brilliant MMO that's well worth jumping into, if you have the time.

Breaking: Nintendo reinstates SmileBasic 4 to the eShop after it was used for Switch 2 jailbreaks

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that smileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop.
  • SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing users to code their own simple programs and games.
  • Technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that smileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop. While the console's firmware has long since been updated to stop known jailbreak exploits, SmileBasic 4 itself has now also been patched.

SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing users to code their own simple programs and games. It's also opened multiple backdoors for jailbreak exploits over the years, first on 3DS, and then on Switch 2.

Technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo. That would allow customers to, in theory, run homebrew applications, but as far as I can tell, the exploit had not yet been extended to allow people to play pirated games.

It has been revealed that nonetheless, Nintendo acted promptly to delist SmileBasic 4 from the eShop and to upgrade the console's firmware to address the exploit at a system level. That's a necessary step, too, as SmileBasic 4 was not the only application that could be used to exploit it. Notably, Civilization 7, a game that is available on cartridge and thus impervious to delistings and software updates, could also be used for the jailbreak.

It has been revealed that even so, it seems that SmileBasic 4 itself has been updated to ensure that a similar exploit never happens again. As Twitter user MarioMasta64 notes, the software itself has gotten a upcoming update post-reinstatement aimed at closing the hole used for the jailbreak. The application's demo – which could also be used to exploit it – has also been updated, but it has not yet been relisted on the eShop.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, after an incredibly long wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has dropped to massively positive reviews from critics, who have repeatedly described Rockstar's latest release as one of, if not the best games ever made. While there was plenty of debate over whether the critic reviews and player responses would actually line up or not when it released, the public response has been almost equally impressive so far.

Despite taking the industry by storm and boasting sales that broke a new record for the entertainment industry, GTA 6's review rating has just plummeted on Metacritic immediately after the site opened its user scores.

As noted by owners like CharlieIntel on X, while there are plenty of user reviews that note the flaws while celebrating its achievements, the User Review section for GTA 6 on Metacritic has been absolutely flooded with overwhelmingly negative reviews, many of which are from players who admit they "haven't even played the game" themselves.

With GTA 6 at the moment sitting at a 5.1 user score at the time of writing, over half of the reviews uploaded for the game are negative, with countless politically charged reviews calling it "woke slop" and a "cuck simulator" over its relationship gameplay mechanics, or people straight-up keyboard-smashing negative reviews just so they can contribute to tearing down the game's score.

While it isn't exactly surprising that one of the most widely talked about games in history would wind up being the target of annoyed players or internet trolls wanting to join in on the fun, Take-Two had already expressed their concern about this exact situation happening years before GTA 6 released.

Even Nintendo's recently released Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake wasn't exempt from the same fate either, with Link's return being slammed by players in response to the game's popularity, rather than the actual quality of the remake.

Considering that there are some genuine complaints to be had surrounding GTA 6's console performance, control scheme, or returning franchise features that are presently absent in the newest release, it's hard to pinpoint what the actual score will end up being after the dust of its release settles.

If the critic scores and the Metacritic rating for Rockstar's previous games are anything to go by, however, Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely wind up with an incredibly high score regardless of the current review bomb storm, especially as the game gets even bigger with the eventual PC port and multiplayer release.

Recent findings suggest that heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which introduced a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

Sources indicate that the first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

In a recent development, the more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your massive reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

We also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox leader Asha Sharma has alluded to harnessing the power of generative AI when making games, in a memo published this afternoon.

Industry observers note that the memo, titled 25 years of Xbox, charts the growth of Microsoft from small beginnings through to the thousands-strong company it is today. But it's Sharma's comments at the end of the memo that are of particular interest.

While talking about what the next 25 years could bring, Sharma lamented that "too many ideas never become games" and that "too many games fall short of what their creators imagined". "For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition," she wrote. "We must change this.".

Sharma continued: "Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

There is no explicit mention of generative AI here, but the language is suggestive - "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations". Furthermore, Asha's memo follows last month's announcement of an Xbox Labs initiative that also sounded like it was based around generative AI, despite avoiding the phrase specifically.

In a recent development, this isn't a surprise, of course. Microsoft as a wider company is all-in on generative AI, with Copilot, and Sharma's background at Microsoft is in AI. But it's an area she's avoided speaking too enthusiastically about since her hiring as Xbox boss earlier this year. At the time, Sharma mentioned she has "no tolerance for bad AI", and there's been such a lot else going on in the months since - including wide-ranging restructuring resulting in the loss of thousands of Xbox jobs - that the topic of generative AI has fallen into the background. Perhaps now we're seeing the sprouting seeds of it.

We've asked Microsoft for clarification.

  • To start, you’ll want to head to the Three Sheers Liquor store, marked on your map by Shirley when you accept her request to snag her rum order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is chock full of side quests that point you towards bonus hits or gang hideouts. All over Leonida, groups of ner’do wells are making cash and leaving it lying around, all yours for the taking if you’re quick enough on the draw and know where to look.

Recent findings suggest that while picking up Jason’s neighbor Shirley’s rum order from a nearby liquor store, you just might hear some squawking the attendant writes off as a loud TV. In reality, he’s hiding a pretty penny within an exotic animal ring run out the back, and a spiteful parrot is stuck back there ready to spill the beans. Let’s go over the quickest way to find it and run it for all its worth.

To start, you’ll want to head to the Three Sheers Liquor store, marked on your map by Shirley when you accept her request to snag her rum order. Located just down the road from Jason’s place, enter for a small cutscene hinting there's more going on behind closed doors.

Once you secure Shirley’s rum in your trunk, head down the alley to the right of the store. You’ll hear a bunch of people arguing with what sounds like a parrot, insulting the crew and blabbing about hiding cash. Continue down the alley until you spot an opening in the barbed wire cover on the wall.

Hop over, and the gang will start a brawl. Be careful, as stepping too far away will prompt multiple members to draw their guns. If you want to get out of this quietly and professionally, make sure you handle the group hand-to-hand; that way, no one calls the cops.

It has been revealed that once you handle all the goons, the parrot will start praising you. By interacting with it, Jason will ask about the money it mentioned, and it will start dropping hints. The important one is the generator, alluding to the small box generator in the upper left corner of the yard, behind the liquor store.

Recent findings suggest that go into focus mode, and you’ll notice a small marked crevice in the side of the store, right beside the generator. Interact with it to pocket a cool $1,382, a solid early-game sum that will more than pay for running Shirley’s errands. You can also pocket a number of melee weapons from the goons, including machetes and shovels if you’re looking for a hand-to-hand option.

The liquor store gang is one of many small, unaffiliated criminal groups that you can find throughout Leonida, acting as a great first taste of the kind of rewards that can be hiding right out of plain sight. Return Shirley’s rum, and you’ve had a very successful errand.

Queen's Domain's melee combat isn't for everyone: Luckily there's an in-game cheat book you can use to get a gun (and it doesn't bork your achievements cheevos or nothin').

First person King's Field/Metroid Prime-like Queen's Domain has rapidly become a top-two shortlister for my personal game of the year, but it can be a prickly, difficult-to-recommend game, particularly in its first 30 minutes or so before you get the game-defining Endu airdash sword.

I'm of a mind with news writer Josh Wolens that the contrast between pre- and post-Endu gameplay really helps sell the game's power curve, but our coworkers Andy Chalk and Morgan Park both bounced off Queen's Domain's admittedly sluggish melee combat.

In a recent development, there isn't a difficulty selection in Queen's Domain, but there is something close to it: A "witch's grimoire" where you can input codes to receive unique items. Most of these are references to streamers, content creators, or other indie developers.

According to recent reports, while referential, they mesh surprisingly well with Queen's Domain's aesthetic, and I don't think they threaten its overall very deliberate sense of progression. What's more, I say playing the game at all is better than avoiding this little cheat code book out of principle.

You can enter the code "hempie" (a reference to the vtuber of the same name) to receive a Soviet SVT-40 semi-automatic battle rifle. A bit incongruous for the medieval fantasy setting, perhaps, but I think it makes for an early game boon while not completely upending Queen's Domain's balance. Most of my preferred later game weapons have been ranged options⁠—the code just gets you one much earlier than you could otherwise. The hempie rifle has already proven an early favorite for Queen's Domain speedrunners like current world record holder Wilbun84, whose video also demonstrates where to find the grimoire.

On the starting beach, you'll notice a dead tree to your right while facing inland. There is a secret compartment on the other side of the tree, facing away from you: Press the "use" button while close to the tree to reveal the secret compartment (similar to the secret doors scattered throughout Queen's Domain). If you'd like to get even crazier with the grimoire, Destructoid has a full list of all the codes you can input with their corresponding rewards. The grimoire has a limited number of uses, so you can't get everything right away, but you can unlock more uses as the game goes on.

Sources indicate that nioh 3 has had a massive weekend on Steam, the type of launch you just don’t often see for Koei Tecmo games. Indeed, this has very clearly been a monumentous release for both the publisher, and developer Team Ninja.

It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

Nioh 3 came out swinging, breaking the series’ Steam concurrent player record immediately after lanch, with 42,822. Anyone keeping up with how well the game has been received, and how much it’s been anticipated by series fans and Soulslike players, would’ve told you that it was only the beginning.

Industry observers note that late on Friday, and several times on Saturday, the game continued achieving new records, setting new peak concurrent levels every couple of hours. It happened again on Sunday, when the game finally settled on its current 88,045 peak concurrent (via SteamDB).

In a recent development, that’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

Last night, Xbox Game Studios and Halo Studios have declared a free patch for the recently-released Halo: Campaign Evolved, which promises to add the four-player co-operative PvE mode, Firefight, to the game.

In a recent development, "For nearly two decades, Firefight has been a Halo favorite, challenging Spartans to team up, hold the line, and survive wave after wave of enemies," says Halo Studios director of competitive engagement Tahir Hasangjekaj stated in a dedicated post on the Xbox website. "The tradition continues this winter as we add the four-player cooperative PvE mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved in a free patch.".

Though we don't have a release date for the update yet, Hasangjekaj does explicitly state "this Winter" as a window, and promises that we'll hear more information about the update at Halo Fest - due to run from 12th to 13hth December in Seattle, Washington. My money would be on a release around then, therefore.

"We're kicking things off tonight at Xbox FanFest, where attendees will be the first to jump in and experience Firefight across latest maps and armed with plenty of weapons to help even the odds." It seems there's already a playable build of the mode, then.

It's worth noting that this is quite an odd news blast from Xbox, since the last official information we heard about the Halo brand was that the next major Halo game being developed by Activision, as Halo Studios all but closes as part of Microsoft's Xbox 'restructuring' that saw one key member behind Halo: Campaign Evolved promoted and laid off within the same week. As things stand, we don't know anything specific about the future of the series, but there are plenty of rumours that the next title will be a reboot developed by Call of Duty's Sledgehammer Games.

Recent findings suggest that it's been fairly busy 24 hours for Xbox: as well as this Halo update, we've heard from Asha Sharma as she celebrated the 25th anniversary of Xbox by seemingly going all-in on Gen AI. Elsewhere, we got the announcement that Wolfenstein 3 is in development over at MachineGames, headed up by Hugo Martin.

How To Deposit Money In A Bank Account In GTA 6

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, living in Leonida isn't cheap, and being a wanted criminal doesn't mean you get to skip the boring financial stuff.
  • Getting your finances in order doesn't require a business degree or a meeting with your accountant.
  • To get a bank account in GTA 6, you'll first need to progress through the main story until you get Lucia out of jail.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, living in Leonida isn't cheap, and being a wanted criminal doesn't mean you get to skip the boring financial stuff. If you've been trying to treat yourself to some new clothes or other goodies in GTA 6, you might have run into a rather annoying little problem: some stores won't let you shop without a bank account. Rude!

Getting your finances in order doesn't require a business degree or a meeting with your accountant. You'll just need to get familiar with the game's banking system and figure out how to manage your cash. Here's everything you need to know to get your money situation sorted.

To get a bank account in GTA 6, you'll first need to progress through the main story until you get Lucia out of jail. Shortly afterward (the day after the first night, in fact), she will call you, asking you to open a bank account.

In a recent development, you'll then visit a bank and speak with the manager, who will explain that he can't open a traditional account for you. Instead, he'll direct you to the BuckMe application. During the cutscene, you'll automatically open the app and set up your account.

Once BuckMe is unlocked, you can deposit your cash at ATMs and use your bank balance to purchase items that require a bank account.

To find the nearest ATM, pull out your phone by pressing up on the D-pad and open the BuckMe application. Select the ATM Locations option (by scrolling down) using the D-pad, and the closest ATM will be marked on your map.

It has been revealed that drive to the location and interact with the ATM to deposit the cash you're carrying into your BuckMe account. You can then use those funds to purchase items at stores that require a bank account.

Industry observers note that buckMe also gives you access to a Family Savings account, which you can transfer money into directly through the application. You'll need to deposit $5,000 into Family Savings to progress through a later quest, so make sure you set aside some money for it while keeping enough in your regular account for shopping.

Sources indicate that some items can still be purchased with physical cash, so you don't need to deposit everything you earn. However, getting BuckMe set up early will make shopping and managing your money much easier throughout GTA 6.

Industry observers note that few things get gamers going more than digital nudity, and plenty of chapters in GTA 6’s leak saga focused on just how naked the residents of Leonida are willing to get. If you followed the leaks, you may remember talk of a nudist resort, well, we managed to find it!

If you want to see some of Leonida’s freest citizens, look no further. We’ve covered exactly where to find the spot, plus everything you can do in this little chunk of paradise.

Recent findings suggest that finding the nudist resort will require you to swing a bit out of the way if you want to find it early, before the main story leads you further out than Hamlet. You’ll want to head northwest, towards Watson Bay along the highway.

As you drive, you’ll eventually pass a small trailer park with a notably heart-shaped pool at its far end. This is the main way to spot the resort from a distance, giving you the chance to pull into the RV park and head down the central path.

In a recent development, sadly, finding the resort is the most exciting part of it, as the actual area is both incredibly small, and doesn’t have anything really unique. The NPCs are notably more chill with either protagonist streaking than most, as you’d expect, but besides a small bar there isn’t much to see.

You can confirm one white whale of the leak era off your checklist at least, and keep your eyes open for more of the quirky little spots that make Leonida so fun to explore.

The Mortality’s Tenderness banner features five new limited-time 5-Star Memories, one each for the game’s five love interests. The theme is all about warmth, reunion, and intimacy, taking place in a Wuxia-inspired setting that's once again an alternate universe from the main story of the game.

The upcoming memory cards are Xavier: Blades with Blossoms, Zayne: Entwined Kites, Rafayel: Carved Gemheart, Sylus: Shared Lanterns, and Caleb: Clearday Return. You can pick three of the five to focus on and further pick one to guarantee on your second 5-star pull; and you can earn wish rewards by making cumulative wishes over the course of the event.

It has been revealed that some of the rewards you could get include limited headwear, Limited Deepspace Wishes, and — of course — Memory-themed outfits and hairstyles inspired by the fresh Memories. Outside of wish rewards, the Memory Series comes with growth tasks that rewards you with in-game materials for levelling up the new cards during the event. When you reach Rank 1 for any new Memory from the banner, you’ll earn a Memory-themed outfit with a special colour that matches your chosen love interest.

Illusio returns as part of the fresh event, too, letting you customise the look of Kindled Moments across all five new Memories. Things you can customise include selecting the outfits and accessories for each love interest, so you can recreate Kindled Moments in your own style. As always, Kindled Moments will go back to their default look after the event ends.

It has been revealed that there’s a latest mini-game to play, too, available only during the event. It’s called Courteous Fare, a frantic but familiar restaurant management simulation that allows you to unlock a variety of rewards.

My firstest-ever Golden Joystick Awards, which took place last night in London, was marred somewhat by 1) a gin & tonic costing eleven quid and 2) my view of the stage being directly obscured by its own rigging. Nonetheless, I did crane enough to get a good view at the reveal of The Sound of Fury, a musically-minded hack 'n' slash in which a troubled classical musician descends into Hell to save a friend from the Devil.

It's not out until late 2027, and the strength of its monster-battering will of course lay in how it feels in the hand. I like the look of this one, though. While it doesn't appear to be a full-on rhythm action game in the Hi-Fi Rush or Dead as Disco vein, it's clearly trying incorporate our glum hero's virtuosity with both visual and thematic flair: spinning attacks are accentuated by trails of sheet music staves, and at least one move inflicts enemies with uncontrollable bouts of dancing. Weapons also take the form of instruments, the trailer being particularly keen to show grand pianos being powerbombed into demon heads. "You dropped your... keys," I will say, to the demons. Heh heh heh.

Also of note is The Sound of Fury's unusual interpretation of Hell, which rather than the usual Biblical/Nordic/Ancient Greek depictions we get in games, is a washed-out mashup of what the Steam page calls "humanity's darkest chapters." Thus, you fight not red-skinned horned imps but gasmasked soldiers and Klu Klux Klansmen, with history-spanning anomalies distorting an otherwise 19th century-flavoured fantasyscape. The laws of time evidently aren't followed here, not least when the protag whips out a Flying V guitar to give the Grim Reaper a different kind of axe wound.

It has been revealed that I can't find much else out about developers and self-publishers Games By Wojtek, with that pluralisation assuming 'they' aren't just one person named Wojtek, but The Sound of Fury looks to be his/their debut game. Hopefully it gets a demo, in due course, so we can try tickling its ivories ourselves.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, as Grand Theft Auto 6 breaks pre-order records on the PlayStation and Xbox stores, and looks poised to break many more sales records once it releases next week, questions of whether it will also break the internet arise.
  • Major game releases register nationally for broadband use: we know this from an investigation into gaming downloads and how much they cost the environment we published in 2021.
  • For this reason, Openreach - the manufacturer that runs the largest broadband network in the UK - has been tracking Rockstar's latest game closely.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as Grand Theft Auto 6 breaks pre-order records on the PlayStation and Xbox stores, and looks poised to break many more sales records once it releases next week, questions of whether it will also break the internet arise. Collective network load will undoubtedly spike around its release - will regional infrastructure be able to bear it?

Major game releases register nationally for broadband use: we know this from an investigation into gaming downloads and how much they cost the environment we published in 2021. We also know that UK communications regulator Ofcom negotiates with gaming companies to try and avoid major game releases happening alongside major cultural occasions, such as sporting events, which are likely to spike broadband use. The network pipes can be clogged, and there's arguably never been a game as anticipated as GTA 6 to clog them.

For this reason, Openreach - the manufacturer that runs the largest broadband network in the UK - has been tracking Rockstar's latest game closely. "GTA 6 has been on our radar for a long time," Trevor Linney, Openreach's director for network technology, told Eurogamer. "We know from games like Fortnite and Call of Duty that a major release or update can drive huge amounts of data across the network, so it'll be fascinating to see just how much GTA moves the needle. Our network and teams are ready, and GTA 6 is certainly one we'll be watching for a newly introduced download record.".

Industry observers note that A spokesperson for Ofcom, meanwhile, said: "Broadband networks should be well placed to handle this download. Ofcom's Broadband Code of Practice means providers must give customers clear, realistic information and guarantee a minimum speed. If you’re not getting this, you may be able to leave your contract penalty-free. Check your speed now, so you can focus on the game rather than the loading screen." Ofcom has a website with sections devoted to broadband speeds and changing providers, in case you're interested.

Alongside yesterday's announcements that GTA 6 had become the most pre-ordered game in Xbox Store and PlayStation Store history, Sony and Microsoft shared strongly worded advice that players download the game ahead of time to avoid complications caused by "unprecedented demand". We saw last year what happened when Hollow Knight: Silksong arrived, causing chaos on Xbox, Steam, and Nintendo servers, and that game's reach was an order of magnitude less than GTA 6's. I don't recall a Selfridges store takeover in London for Silksong - do you?

The wait for GTA 6 is finally nearly over, as it arrives next Thursday, 19th November.

#75126. What Is The Day/Night Cycle Length In GTA 6?

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (411 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

What Is The Day/Night Cycle Length In GTA 6?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (411 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every day in Grand Theft Auto 6 is relatively long, but it's not as long as real life.
  • The same goes for days that are too long, though, since it wouldn't be realistic for it to take only an hour or so to drive all the way around the entire state.
  • Recent findings suggest that every minute in Grand Theft Auto 6 lasts for five real seconds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every day in Grand Theft Auto 6 is relatively long, but it's not as long as real life. A day has to be long enough to do some of the many things in the game, but it also has to reflect the size of the map. If you drove from one end of the map to the other, it wouldn't be realistic if it took you multiple days just to drive across the city.

The same goes for days that are too long, though, since it wouldn't be realistic for it to take only an hour or so to drive all the way around the entire state. Luckily, we did the math to determine just how long a day is in Leonida.

Recent findings suggest that every minute in Grand Theft Auto 6 lasts for five real seconds. That means every hour lasts 300 seconds, or five real-life minutes. With the same conversion for a 24-hour day, multiply that five minutes by 24, and you find that a full 24-hour cycle in the game lasts for two real-life hours.

This is significantly longer than a day in Grand Theft Auto 5, which lasted 48 real-life minutes. The scaling makes sense, though, because the map size matches each day's length. If a day in GTA 5 lasted as long as it did in GTA 6, you could've crossed the map multiple times in a single cycle.

Recent findings suggest that while you can't directly speed up the clocks, you can skip chunks of time if you don't want to be out at a certain time. If you go to bed, you can choose to sleep, and setting your alarm will determine what time of day it is when you get up.

You can set the alarm for morning, noon, evening, or night. It doesn't matter what time you go to sleep; you can sleep until any time of day. If it's earlier than it currently is, it will move on to the next in-game day. That way, if you have tasks that depend on a certain time of day or require you to wait for the next day, you can skip the wait.

Luckily, there's plenty to do day or night in this game, and certain events only happen at certain times. It's good to know you can skip time if you need to, but there are lots of reasons to enjoy the day/night cycle to the fullest.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox boss Asha Sharma has confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in development at MachineGames, the Swedish studio behind the acclaimed Wolfenstein: The Upcoming Order, Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossal, and 2024's celebrated Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. Additionally, she revealed Doom developer idSoftware - one of the Microsoft-owned studios heavily impacted by sweeping Xbox job cuts earlier this year - is now working on a new game.

Sharma has, of course, been on a bit of a PR offensive of late, positioning herself alongside snippets of positive news at a time Xbox is embroiled in a massive business "reset" effort that has resulted in proposed studio closures and mass layoffs that will ultimately see 3,200 Xbox employees lose their jobs. This week's Wolfenstein 3 reveal similarly arrived in the form of a tweet posted directly from her social media account.

Recent findings suggest that "Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames," Sharma wrote on X. "One of gaming's most vital franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more." As for idSoftware's upcoming project, confirmation of that - again attributed directly to Sharma - appeared in a post on Bethesda's website. "Slaughter Mode comes to Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations on Monday," she wrote, "and the team is already working on its next game.".

In July, sweeping job cuts at Xbox resulted in 96 of idSoftware's 136 employees being laid off in a move one former team member described as a "bloodbath". Since then, idSoftware co-studio director Marty Stratton has attempted to downplay the cuts, recently insisting the studio was "doing great". He added id was "working more closely than ever" with MachineGames - a studio which appears to have escaped Sharma's restructuring efforts so far.

This week's Wolfenstein and idSoftware news follows similar efforts by Xbox to reassure fans their favourite franchises are unaffected by the recent layoffs. Shortly after substantial job cuts at Bethesda were confirmed, the company moved to insist The Elder Scrolls 6 was still "on the way" and that its plans were "unaffected" (the company has since released a trailer announcing its subtitle). It also confirmed a new Fallout game was in development.

Xbox's year of bad news - which includes ongoing boycott efforts relating to Microsoft's controversial involvement with the Israeli military - comes as the division celebrates its 25th anniversary. Earlier this week, Sharma shared a memo to staff marking the occasion, albeit one in which she seemingly championed a gen-AI future for games development, enthusing that, "A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers".

According to recent reports, this doesn't seem to be kid fodder, though. Lola's a bean but the familiars, and the prison's other denizens, are growling towers of jaws and decaying flesh. Developers Caracal Games are promising they'll star in a "heartfelt and emotionally resonant story about growth," to balance out the grimness, though I'm less clear on a following blurb point that declares it a "lite-vania," into which you'll "dive into exploration, trial-and-error and platforming, without feeling frustrated." While this might just be an attempt to assuage fears that this'll a Hollow Knight- or Nine Sols-style controller-thrower, I do wonder how one goes light on 'vania. Maybe some of the ability gates open if you just ask them nicely?

That aside, I'm already quite charmed by Lola's Familiars, especially the designs of its bag-eyed wallflower of a heroine and her contrastingly hench minions. Release date is TBC, but the Steam page is up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most hotly anticipated games of all time, and few things can slow down its momentum, thanks to the sheer hype and quality on display. The quickest thing to put a damper on excitement, sadly, is bugs, hiccups that are both unintended and hard to fix in any quick manner.

The streets of Leonida have been plagued by a number of minor graphical and physics bugs that have led to laughs, but one repeat offender is causing complications for PS5 players. Internally titled error code CE-108255-1, this bug causes a no-frills, hard crash back to the PlayStation home screen after a brief play window, causing players to lose progress and time as they’re forced to reset.

According to recent reports, for a massive open-world story game like Grand Theft Auto 6, forced short playtimes can be a killer, and the constant crashes forced by error code CE-108255-1 are causing just that. Complaints across the internet say the error has no discernible cause, but it only appears on PlayStation 5 systems, leaving Xbox players in the clear.

A recent set of firmware updates could be causing the error afflicting PS5 players, but neither Sony nor Rockstar has released any statement on it. Hopefully, as more players stumble into it, a swift hotfix patches the glitch before too many lose potentially hours of playtime to a simple bug. GTA6’s robust simulation elements would make the loss even harder, taking tons of hard work with it.

According to recent reports, no usual methods seem to help; reinstalling the game, going offline, and keeping the system cool all seem to be fruitless. Without a proper fix, players are stuck just hoping it doesn’t happen to them, a frustrating possibility that could easily tarnish their experience playing such an anticipated release.

The quickest thing to put a damper on excitement, sadly, is bugs, hiccups that are both unintended and hard to fix in any quick manner.

In a recent development, across the board, Grand Theft Auto 6 seems very well optimized, despite being trapped at 30 FPS across all platforms. A frame unlock is likely to come with the PC version, either officially or thanks to mods once the title jumps ship from consoles. Until then, fans are forced to pray and keep playing, crossing their fingers that their hard-earned cash isn’t lost due to the whims of an error they can’t avoid.

Industry observers note that over the last decade or so, a number of massive AAA titles have been released frankly unfinished. With Cyberpunk 2077 as the biggest offender, players have gotten sick and tired of being forced to shuffle through mountains of bugs and errors in order to play the games they pay for.

That makes Grand Theft Auto 6’s error code CE-108255-1 all the more frustrating; with how well polished the vast majority of the experience is, a hiccup like this sticks out like a sore thumb. The fine folks at Rockstar have clearly spent over a decade of blood, sweat, and tears to make Grand Theft Auto 6 the powerhouse it is, and losing face because of a bug like this is just sad.

With no acknowledgement from the studio yet, fans are left to their own devices, and some have gotten more than a little spiteful.

No physical copy, a $79.99 base price tag, and multiple on-disc locations barred behind a special edition give GTA6 an outer coat that has nothing to do with its criminal focus. It feels like the industry is yet again at a tipping point set by a significant player, with the future in the hands of the rest of the AAA developers surrounding them.

  • According to recent reports, I'm not a huge GTA guy, but I am a Red Dead head.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every time the very concept of a GTA 6 has come up in the past eight years, I've had just one wistful opinion to contribute: "I hope they make it more like Red Dead Redemption 2.".

According to recent reports, I'm not a huge GTA guy, but I am a Red Dead head. The sequel is Rockstar's best work (maybe second best now?) because of all the ways it prioritizes roleplay and choice-making by simulating the little things: Mixing tonics, crafting bullets individually, grooming Arthur's mustache. God, I love that stuff.

There was no way Rockstar would repeat all of these life sim-y touches for the louder and faster GTA 6, but I am surprised and elated that my favorite Red Dead 2 feature of them all made the cut: Your car is your horse.

Recent findings suggest that that is to say, Jason and Lucia's personal vehicles are their mobile bases—an essential extension of them. You can't pet or name it, sadly, but it's key to keep track of and take care of your whip, because it's where you keep all your guns and outfits. It's all literally in the trunk: If you want to fetch your shotgun, you have to walk to the back of the car, open it up, and fish it out of a box.

In a recent development, gone are the days of keeping seven assault rifles, ten SMGs, and four rocket launchers in your back pocket—you can only equip two "long" guns on your back, and large melee weapons like bats have to be stowed away, too. Aside from how cool it is to fish a shotgun out of my trunk like a disgruntled Jason Statham character, the limitation is forcing me to think twice about how to approach missions.

Industry observers note that and unlike in Red Dead's lawless towns, the NPCs of Leonida seem to react negatively to the guy walking around with assault rifles on his back. The game tells you early on that police pay closer attention to you when openly carrying firearms—another reason to stow them away when you don't need 'em.

Industry observers note that the car trunk is also where extra outfits can be stored. You can bring along five by default (more than Red Dead's saddles allowed), and even this isn't just for vanity. GTA 6's wanted system goes further than police chases: if you lose the cops, your wanted level will linger and cops identify you based on your description, clothes, and your car. The easiest way to go incognito after raising cain is to pull over, pop the trunk, and change outfits.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

In a recent development, it's all very smart and cool and I love it. Though I can also understand why others wouldn't—it's a significant break from what GTA has been up to this point. The two gun limit means murderous rampages might end earlier than they used to, and I can foresee getting annoyed the first time I bring a sniper rifle to a shotgun fight and have no way to correct that. But I think this reflects how Rockstar designed GTA 6 to be just as much a life sim as a crime fantasy.

GTA 6 wants me to constantly make choices and consider what a real human would do. Like in one mission last night, I was left alone without my personal vehicle for the first time. Instead of Rockstar suggesting I grand theft an auto, a tutorial popped for calling a cab. So yea, I took a yellow cab back to my car a few miles away, and it was a chill ride, except for the cabbie who rudely shot down my attempts to make small talk. He's lucky my guns were in my car.

I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game. Obviously there are plenty of genres that are trendy to imitate, but how often do you see something that's just sort of "thing you know slapped on top of game you know?" Perhaps that's a tad mean, but I do genuinely have a fondness for such games, so I'm quite pleased by the announcement of Conan: The Black Pyramid, an action roguelite RPG that so clearly went to Supergiant Games' School of Hades you have to admire the boldness just a little bit.

Industry observers note that conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more! So, immediately, a notable enough difference from Hades, and one that seems like a neat take. As one of them you then "Descend into eldritch chambers of the Black Pyramid, a mysterious and dangerous place that defies the logic of space and time. Confront the shadows of the champions themselves and piece together the dark secrets of their past.".

Sources indicate that where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest. Each character has their own combination of weapons and abilities, so it does sound like you can mix it up quite nicely. There is, also, 2-player online co-op (sorry to the couch lovers, I suppose), adding to the ways it differs and making it a tad more friendly for those that have exactly one friend who also loves Conan.

Overall, seems like a fresh enough take on Hades while still trying to find some amount of its own identity. And hey, Hades is great, so I'm never upset about having a little bit more of that kind of game. No release date attached to Conan: The Black Pyramid just yet, but it is planned to arrive sometime in 2027. You can check it out on Steam here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the newly introduced content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a upcoming blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing challenges with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

Industry observers note that we know that Season 2 is introducing a substantial fresh map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

Sources indicate that the real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the fresh season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

It has been revealed that challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

Industry observers note that BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

According to recent reports, movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Sources indicate that audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that slay the Spire 2, which released into early access earlier this year, is expanding once more with a major newly introduced beta update. This introduces the deckbuilder's first new character since launch - a whimsical musician armed with a bow - alongside two new modes, and more.

It has been revealed that when Slay the Spire 2 arrived back in March, it was to much enthusiastic acclaim. Eurogamer's Bertie Purchie is a substantial fan, and has trumpeted its successes on multiple occasions, calling the sequel's co-op mode "transformative". And it was a commercial hit too, managing to shift over 5m copies in just a month of release. All of which means there are plenty of eyes on Slay the Spire 2, eager to see what developer MegaCrit does next.

Industry observers note that so far major updates have brought the likes of buffs, balance adjustments, art updates, UI improvements, bug fixes, and more - and MegaCrit has also made other substantial adjustments including the jettisoning of third act boss Doormaker, after it decided the encounter was overly complex. And now, as 2026 nears its conclusion, the studio has released its "biggest (beta) patch yet", including a sweep of major additions.

As per MegaCrit's v0.113.0 patch notes, the headliner is The Fool; Slay the Spire 2's first new character, who's described as a "silly musician who wields a bow". Unsurprisingly, The Fool doesn't arrive in their final form, and the studio says it expects to make a "great number of content and balance changes" before the character is ready for the main branch.

Accompanying The Fool are two new game modes: Blitz and Dread. Blitz is described as a "condensed and chaotic" mode focused on deckbuilding. Unlocked after completing an Ascension run of any difficulty, it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across all characters. "The Merchant's wares feel a bit off," MegaCrit teases, "the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters??".

In a recent development, if you're looking for a more gruelling challenge, though, there's the "brutally difficult" newly introduced Dread mode, designed for players who've reached Ascension 10 on all characters, including The Fool. All ascension modifiers are enabled, according to MegaCrit, while bosses are stronger and buff all enemies found across their Act. And if that's still not enough to get your heart racing, MegaCrit notes curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire.

In a recent development, beyond the headline stuff, v0.113.0 tweaks rest sites so they appear one floor earlier every act, and that's alongside the usual list of UI changes, art additions, nerfs, balance adjustments, and more. Full patch notes can be found on Steam.

Recent findings suggest that those players eager to put Slay the Spire 2's latest additions through their paces will need to enable the beta branch by right-clicking on Slay the Spire 2 in their Steam library and navigating to Properties > Game Versions & Betas and selecting 'public-beta' from the dropdown menu. MegaCrit notes the game's main branch has also been updated with all content and changes from the previous beta.

  • While these tasks are optional, they will make Lucia happy and earn you points in your relationship.
  • In a recent development, as all homeowners know, the work is never truly done to make the place perfectly livable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, at the start of Grand Theft Auto 6, when Jason gets a call from Lucia saying she's getting out of prison, he realizes there's a lot to do around the house to get it ready for her arrival. He notices the leaks in the roof, and it turns out that there's plenty more to do to get the place in shape.

While these tasks are optional, they will make Lucia happy and earn you points in your relationship. While they're relatively easy quick-time events, it's important to do them so Lucia feels welcome as soon as she's finally out of the slammer.

In a recent development, as all homeowners know, the work is never truly done to make the place perfectly livable. Jason swiftly learns that, having to fix numerous problems, but it's worth it if it makes Lucia feel at home. He has to fix the roof, the railing by the gym equipment, the front stairs, and, most importantly, the bedroom.

To fix up Jason's roof, head out the front door of the house, and you'll see a yellow ladder leaning against the wall to the right of the door. Climb up and walk over to the gap in the shingles. You'll get a prompt to interact with them, and you'll have to nail them on by pulling the trigger when prompted.

To repair the stairs, go to the bottom of the front steps, which end right by where Jason parks his car. At the bottom, you'll see a large pile of boards sitting next to the stairs, and when they aren't fixed, you'll notice they creak when you walk on them.

Sources indicate that interact with the boards to fix the stairs. Pull off the old steps by pulling the triggers, then use the right trigger to nail them down properly.

To fix the railing, go to where Jason has his squat rack set up on the deck. You'll see a gap in the slats, and when you're standing at the level of the workout equipment, you'll get a prompt to repair it.

Make sure you're on the lower level of the deck, as the prompt won't appear from the top.

According to recent reports, jason will then start taking the wooden posts and nailing them in place; you can do this by pulling the trigger when prompted. After a few of these, the railing will look nice and neat for Lucia.

Possibly one of the more memed parts of the early game so far, Jason needs to fix up the bedroom to make it feel like home. Go into the bedroom, go to the panel of drywall leaning against the wooden frame and interact with the prompt to start the repair.

Recent findings suggest that first, he'll fit the drywall, and you'll need to use the trigger to nail the wall into place. Then, after a cutscene of him filling those nail holes, you'll get to choose the color. Once you have, you'll be prompted to move the joystick up and down to paint the walls and finish the room.

After those four tasks are completed, Lucia will feel much more at home once she gets there, which will make her happy. Of course, that, along with adding a bit of Feng Shui, will make the place really start to feel like home.

Speaking of fanboying, if you're a fan of cheesy Hollywood blockbusters, you may have enjoyed the original Fast and Furious movies. If so, I have a surprise for you. The madmen at Rockstar have added Brian’s (Paul Walker) Eclipse to GTA 6 as an Easter Egg, and it is an absolute thing of beauty.

So, if you want to know more about where you can rapidly find this car and own it for yourself, then join me for this brief guide for GTA 6, where I’ll discuss the location of the iconic green Eclipse from the first Fast and Furious movie, as well as how you can own it.

Note: I strongly recommend being in Chapter 2 when you try to get this car; you’ll see why.

Recent findings suggest that more specifically, this is a modified Penumbra, which looks almost identical to the iconic '95 Eclipse from the Fast and Furious franchise. You can find this specialized car at the dead center of Vespucci Islands, located in the heart of Vice City.

Recent findings suggest that the location is shown above, so make your way over; the exact spot is a house with a locked fence gate you can climb over. Either just open the garage or go through the side door to find the modified Penumbra with the unique livery.

Sources indicate that and much like the buster that got Dom out of handcuffs in the movie, you’ll have to break open and hotwire the car to steal it for yourself here. It will set off an alarm that will alert nearby residents and eventually the cops, so I strongly advise you to get the car out of there immediately.

According to recent reports, of course, if you’re in Chapter 1, you won’t have an option to own or register another car as Jason. However, once you make it to Chapter 2, you can register a car with Lucia after you first visit a guy named Moses at a garage. This is where I strongly recommend you get this car because the first one you register with Moses is free of charge, as long as the car you bring is low-key.

It has been revealed that the Green ’95 Eclipse Penumbra will work without any problems, so you can bring it straight back to his garage and get this beauty owned under Lucia. But there’s a slight catch that may rub you the wrong way.

Industry observers note that registering this car as your first free one from Moses means you have to wipe the livery off and replace it with a standard paint job. Don’t panic; it may look like you can’t recover the iconic livery, but you actually can: just visit the Vice Vinyl Mod shop in Vice City, and this garage should give you the option to restore the car's original livery/paint job.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after the Clean Up After Donnie GTA 6 mission, Donnie becomes a fence you can sell narcotics, marked notes, and jewelry to, all you have to do is drop them in the deposit box at his trailer in Key Lento. But with Brian also a fence, you may be wondering whether it's more beneficial to sell your goods to Donnie or Brian. While one may offer more lucrative rewards, all that glitters isn't necessarily gold in GTA 6.

It has been revealed that if you hover your cursor over a fencing location icon on the GTA 6 map, you can see the rate each respective fence is offering for narcotics, marked bills, and jewelry. In GTA 6 Chapter 1, Donnie (Donnie's Trailer) pays low for narcotics, and very low for jewelry and marked bills.

Brian (Brian's Lockup), on the other hand, pays very low for all three types of illicit products. As such, Donnie pays more than Brian for narcotics. For example, if you collect all the cocaine drops Cal tells you about after the Clean Up After Donnie mission and fence them, Donnie offers you $3,400, while Brian offers just $2,720. Do note that the time it takes for these payments to reach your mailbox can be impacted by any available missions.

Sources indicate that while Donnie pays more, Cal suggests you sell the cocaine drops you collect to Brian, by depositing them at Brian's Lockup in Key Lento. He doesn't say why, but he seems to know something you don't. You should listen to Cal and sell your goods to Brian as the events of a later mission, called Swamped, might impact any payments Donnie owes you in GTA 6 (be aware of major spoilers by following that link).

Note that if you sell to Brian and he seems to be taking his time to pay you, there may be an available Brian mission you must complete before your payment is sent to the mailbox at Jason's House.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, even though it feels like NCIS: Origins just premiered on the 2026 TV schedule, the series is already winding down its third season. Along with a few other CBS highlights, Origins’ season was cut short due to scheduling. Instead of a full season, it’s only getting ten episodes and will be replaced by NCIS: Sydney in January, which is also getting just ten episodes. Now, with the Season 3 finale fast approaching, Kyle Schmid is very passionate about getting a Season 4 renewal, but his words don’t exactly reassure me.

Recent findings suggest that the NCIS prequel is only three seasons in, but it’s definitely become a favorite among fans. And with Mark Harmon back as Leroy Jethro Gibbs for all of Season 3, these new episodes are better than ever. And the hope for a fourth season is getting stronger. Unfortunately, there’s no telling when CBS could be making a decision, so Schmid is jumping on the campaign train. The Mike Franks actor told TV Insider just how much the show, crew, and cast deserve another season, and I desperately need it:.

In a recent development, the show is exceptional this year. I’m so proud of the writing team, our cast, our crew, everybody that I had the pleasure of working with for the past four or five months. I think we found our thing this year. I think the show’s found its shape. I think the characters have found their meaning.

It has been revealed that as a day one Origins fan, I would love nothing more than to never see this show end, especially because it’s gotten better the longer it’s been on. Even with fewer episodes, Origins has been pumping out some great storylines, and that’s going to continue until the very end of Season 3. Plus, while Schmid couldn’t go into detail about what’s to come, his comments make it clear that Origins cannot end any time soon:.

And let me tell you, when I say I don’t want the show to end like this, the show can’t end like this, and I mean that with all my fucking heart. So when you get to the finale of the show, you will know damn well what I mean when I say it cannot go out like this, so there better be a Season fucking 4.

Industry observers note that this has me very concerned, because Schmid is implying that we're going to be dying to see what happens after Season 3 ends. And let me tell you, I absolutely hate cliffhangers, and I hold grudges against them when shows are canceled right after one, because I know we'll never get a resolution. So, if Origins ends in a way that leaves me ravenous for more, it better not get axed.

It has been revealed that now, I can't say I'm shocked that we probably need to prepare for a brutal cliffhanger. If NCIS: Origins is great at one thing, it’s ending seasons on them. Season 1’s finale saw Lala getting into a car crash, while Season 2 ended with Randy getting abducted. If Season 3 follows the pattern and ends on a cliffhanger, which it sounds like it will, a cancellation would be heartbreaking.

CBS has confirmed that the Season 3 finale of NCIS: Origins will premiere on January 19, so fans will see just what Schmid is talking about in two months. I am also passionate about the show getting another season, and if the finale is as substantial as it sounds, I will be hopping on the campaign train with the actor.

For now, fans will just have to wait and see what happens. The series is currently off for the Thanksgiving holiday, but newly introduced episodes will be back on Tuesday, December 1, on CBS, streaming the next day with a Paramount+ subscription.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4’s segment in the major Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

Industry observers note that the Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

It has been revealed that the livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the fresh class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

In a recent development, what we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Looks, and Echoing Hatred.

War Aims lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a upcoming activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

Industry observers note that we also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

It has been revealed that the Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first fresh class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.
